नमन्संवर्णयन्भक्त्या संस्मरन्प्रेमविह्वलः ॥

2.1.s:
brahmalokaṃ jagāmātha śivasmaraṇasanmatiḥ |
śivatattvaṃ viśeṣeṇa jñātumicchuḥ sa nāradaḥ ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मलोकं जगामाथ शिवस्मरणसन्मतिः ।
शिवतत्त्वं विशेषेण ज्ञातुमिच्छुः स नारदः ॥

2.1.s:
natvā tatra vidhiṃ bhaktyā stutvā ca vividhaistavaiḥ |
papraccha śivasattattvaṃ śivasaṃyuktamānasaḥ ||
2.1.d:
नत्वा तत्र विधिं भक्त्या स्तुत्वा च विविधैस्तवैः ।
पप्रच्छ शिवसत्तत्त्वं शिवसंयुक्तमानसः ॥

2.1.s:
nārada uvāca |
brahmanbrahmasvarūpajña pitāmaha jagatprabho |
tvatprasādānmayā sarvaṃ viṣṇormāhātmyamuttamam ||
2.1.d:
नारद उवाच ।
ब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मस्वरूपज्ञ पितामह जगत्प्रभो ।
त्वत्प्रसादान्मया सर्वं विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥

2.1.s:
bhaktimārgaṃ jñānamārgaṃ tapomārgaṃ sudustaram |
dānamārgaṃ ca tīrthānāṃ mārgaṃ ca śrutavānaham ||
2.1.d:
भक्तिमार्गं ज्ञानमार्गं तपोमार्गं सुदुस्तरम् ।
दानमार्गं च तीर्थानां मार्गं च श्रुतवानहम् ॥

2.1.s:
na jñātaṃ śivatattvaṃ ca pūjāvidhimataḥ kramāt |
caritraṃ vividhaṃ tasya nivedaya mama prabho ||
2.1.d:
न ज्ञातं शिवतत्त्वं च पूजाविधिमतः क्रमात् ।
चरित्रं विविधं तस्य निवेदय मम प्रभो ॥

2.1.s:
nirguṇo'pi śivastāta saguṇaḥ śaṅkaraḥ katham |
śivatattvaṃ na jānāmi mohitaḥ śivamāyayā ||
2.1.d:
निर्गुणोऽपि शिवस्तात सगुणः शङ्करः कथम् ।
शिवतत्त्वं न जानामि मोहितः शिवमायया ॥

2.1.s:
sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ kathaṃ śambhuḥ svarūpeṇa pratiṣṭhitaḥ |
sṛṣṭimadhye sa hi kathaṃ krīḍansaṃvartate prabhuḥ ||
2.1.d:
सृष्टेः पूर्वं कथं शम्भुः स्वरूपेण प्रतिष्ठितः ।
सृष्टिमध्ये स हि कथं क्रीडन्संवर्तते प्रभुः ॥

2.1.s:
tadante ca kathaṃ devaḥ sa tiṣṭhati maheśvaraḥ |
kathaṃ prasannatāṃ yāti śaṅkaro lokaśaṅkaraḥ ||
2.1.d:
तदन्ते च कथं देवः स तिष्ठति महेश्वरः ।
कथं प्रसन्नतां याति शङ्करो लोकशङ्करः ॥

2.1.s:
santuṣṭaśca svabhaktebhyaḥ parebhyaśca maheśvaraḥ |
kiṃ phalaṃ yacchati vidhe tatsarvaṃ kathayasva me ||
2.1.d:
सन्तुष्टश्च स्वभक्तेभ्यः परेभ्यश्च महेश्वरः ।
किं फलं यच्छति विधे तत्सर्वं कथयस्व मे ॥

2.1.s:
sadyaḥ prasanno bhagavānbhavatītyanusaṃśrutam |
bhaktaprayāsaṃ sa mahānna paśyati dayāparaḥ ||
2.1.d:
सद्यः प्रसन्नो भगवान्भवतीत्यनुसंश्रुतम् ।
भक्तप्रयासं स महान्न पश्यति दयापरः ॥

2.1.s:
brahmā viṣṇurmaheśaśca trayo devāḥ śivāṃśajāḥ |
maheśastatra pūrṇāṃśaḥ svayameva śivaḥ paraḥ ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मा विष्णुर्महेशश्च त्रयो देवाः शिवांशजाः ।
महेशस्तत्र पूर्णांशः स्वयमेव शिवः परः ॥

2.1.s:
tasyāvirbhāvamākhyāhi caritāni viśeṣataḥ |
umāvirbhāvamākhyāhi tadvivāhaṃ tathā vibho ||
2.1.d:
तस्याविर्भावमाख्याहि चरितानि विशेषतः ।
उमाविर्भावमाख्याहि तद्विवाहं तथा विभो ॥

2.1.s:
tadgārhasthyaṃ viśeṣeṇa tathā līlāḥ parā api |
etatsarvaṃ tathānyacca kathanīyaṃ tvayānagha ||
2.1.d:
तद्गार्हस्थ्यं विशेषेण तथा लीलाः परा अपि ।
एतत्सर्वं तथान्यच्च कथनीयं त्वयानघ ॥

2.1.s:
tadutpattiṃ vivāhaṃ ca śivāyāstu viśeṣataḥ |
prabrūhi me prajānātha guhajanma tathaiva ca ||
2.1.d:
तदुत्पत्तिं विवाहं च शिवायास्तु विशेषतः ।
प्रब्रूहि मे प्रजानाथ गुहजन्म तथैव च ॥

2.1.s:
bahubhyaśca śrutaṃ pūrvaṃ na tṛpto'smi jagatprabho |
atastvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptaḥ kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari ||
2.1.d:
बहुभ्यश्च श्रुतं पूर्वं न तृप्तोऽस्मि जगत्प्रभो ।
अतस्त्वां शरणं प्राप्तः कृपां कुरु ममोपरि ॥

2.1.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasya nāradasyāṅgajasya hi |
uvāca vacanaṃ tatra brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaḥ sṛṣṭikhaṇḍaḥ
2.1.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य नारदस्याङ्गजस्य हि ।
उवाच वचनं तत्र ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां प्रथमः सृष्टिखण्डः
2.1.m:
Homage to glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

The first Creation Section in the second Rudrasaṃhitā.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
bho brahmansādhu pṛṣṭo'haṃ tvayā vibudhasattama |
lokopakāriṇā nityaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
भो ब्रह्मन्साधु पृष्टोऽहं त्वया विबुधसत्तम ।
लोकोपकारिणा नित्यं लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / O Brahmin, O best among the wise, you have questioned me well, / you who always bring benefit to the world, wishing for the welfare of all people.

2.1.s:
yacchrutvā sarvalokānāṃ sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet |
tadahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi śivatattvamanāmayam ||
2.1.d:
यच्छ्रुत्वा सर्वलोकानां सर्वपापक्षयो भवेत् ।
तदहं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि शिवतत्त्वमनामयम् ॥
2.1.m: Hearing which all the sins of all beings are destroyed, / that flawless truth of Śiva I shall tell you.

2.1.s:
śivatattvaṃ mayā naiva viṣṇunāpi yathārthataḥ |
jñātaṃ ca paramaṃ rūpamadbhutaṃ ca pareṇa na ||
2.1.d:
शिवतत्त्वं मया नैव विष्णुनापि यथार्थतः ।
ज्ञातं च परमं रूपमद्भुतं च परेण न ॥
2.1.m: The truth of Śiva has not in reality been known by me, / nor by Viṣṇu, nor has that supreme and wonderful form been known by anyone else.

2.1.s:
mahāpralayakāle ca naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame |
āsīttamomayaṃ sarvamanarkagrahatārakam ||
acandramanahorātramanagnyanilabhūjalam |
apradhānaṃ viyacchūnyamanyatejovivarjitam ||
2.1.d:
महाप्रलयकाले च नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ।
आसीत्तमोमयं सर्वमनर्कग्रहतारकम् ॥
अचन्द्रमनहोरात्रमनग्न्यनिलभूजलम् ।
अप्रधानं वियच्छून्यमन्यतेजोविवर्जितम् ॥
2.1.m:
And at the time of the great dissolution, when mobile and immobile beings had vanished, / everything was shrouded in darkness, without sun, planets, or stars.

Without moon, without day or night, without fire, wind, earth, or water, / without the unmanifest source, a void space deprived of any other light.

2.1.s:
adṛṣṭatvādirahitaṃ śabdasparśasamujjhitam |
avyaktagandharūpaṃ ca rasatyaktamadiṅmukham ||
2.1.d:
अदृष्टत्वादिरहितं शब्दस्पर्शसमुज्झितम् ।
अव्यक्तगन्धरूपं च रसत्यक्तमदिङ्मुखम् ॥
2.1.m: Free from unseen fate and the rest, entirely devoid of sound and touch, / without manifest smell or form, devoid of taste, lacking directions.

2.1.s:
itthaṃ satyandhatamase sūcībhedye nirantare |
tatsadbrahmeti yacchrutvā sadekaṃ pratipadyate ||
2.1.d:
इत्थं सत्यन्धतमसे सूचीभेद्ये निरन्तरे ।
तत्सद्ब्रह्मेति यच्छ्रुत्वा सदेकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
2.1.m: When there was such pitch darkness, dense and impenetrable as a needle, / that which is called "the existent Brahman", of which one hears, is apprehended as the single Existent.

2.1.s:
itīdṛśaṃ yadā nāsīdyattatsadasadātmakam |
yogino'ntarhitākāśe yatpaśyanti nirantaram ||
2.1.d:
इतीदृशं यदा नासीद्यत्तत्सदसदात्मकम् ।
योगिनोऽन्तर्हिताकाशे यत्पश्यन्ति निरन्तरम् ॥
2.1.m: When there was no such thing as consists of existence and nonexistence, / that which yogins constantly see in the space hidden within,

2.1.s:
amanogocaraṃ vācāṃ viṣayaṃ na kadācana |
anāmarūpavarṇaṃ ca na ca sthūlaṃ na yatkṛśam ||
2.1.d:
अमनोगोचरं वाचां विषयं न कदाचन ।
अनामरूपवर्णं च न च स्थूलं न यत्कृशम् ॥
2.1.m: inaccessible to the mind, never an object of words, / without name, form, or colour, neither gross nor subtle,

2.1.s:
ahrasvadīrghamalaghu gurutvaparivarjitam |
na yatropacayaḥ kaścittathā nopacayo'pi ca ||
2.1.d:
अह्रस्वदीर्घमलघु गुरुत्वपरिवर्जितम् ।
न यत्रोपचयः कश्चित्तथा नोपचयोऽपि च ॥
2.1.m: neither short nor long, neither light nor endowed with heaviness, / wherein there is no increase whatsoever, nor any decrease either,

2.1.s:
abhidhatte sacakitaṃ yadastīti śrutiḥ punaḥ |
satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ ca parānandaṃ paraṃ mahaḥ ||
2.1.d:
अभिधत्ते सचकितं यदस्तीति श्रुतिः पुनः ।
सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं च परानन्दं परं महः ॥
2.1.m: which the Vedic revelation designates with awe, saying again, "It is," / truth, knowledge, the infinite, supreme bliss, the supreme light,

2.1.s:
aprameyamanādhāramavikāramanākṛti |
nirguṇaṃ yogigamyaṃ ca sarvavyāpyekakārakam ||
2.1.d:
अप्रमेयमनाधारमविकारमनाकृति ।
निर्गुणं योगिगम्यं च सर्वव्याप्येककारकम् ॥
2.1.m: immeasurable, without support, changeless, formless, / devoid of qualities, accessible to yogins, all-pervasive, the sole cause,

2.1.s:
nirvikalpaṃ nirārambhaṃ nirmāyaṃ nirupadravam |
advitīyamanādyantamavikāśaṃ cidātmakam ||
2.1.d:
निर्विकल्पं निरारम्भं निर्मायं निरुपद्रवम् ।
अद्वितीयमनाद्यन्तमविकाशं चिदात्मकम् ॥
2.1.m: without conceptual construction, without beginning, free from illusion, free from affliction, / without a second, without origin or end, without expansion, consisting of consciousness—

2.1.s:
yasyetthaṃ saṃvikalpante saṃjñāsaṃjñoktitaḥ sma vai |
kiyatā caiva kālena dvitīyecchā'bhavatkila ||
2.1.d:
यस्येत्थं संविकल्पन्ते संज्ञासंज्ञोक्तितः स्म वै ।
कियता चैव कालेन द्वितीयेच्छाऽभवत्किल ॥
2.1.m: when regarding that [Brahman] diverse notions thus arose through designations and their meanings, / after some time, indeed, the desire for a second arose.

2.1.s:
amūrtena svamūrtiśca tenākalpi svalīlayā |
sarvaiśvaryaguṇopetā sarvajñānamayī śubhā ||
2.1.d:
अमूर्तेन स्वमूर्तिश्च तेनाकल्पि स्वलीलया ।
सर्वैश्वर्यगुणोपेता सर्वज्ञानमयी शुभा ॥
2.1.m: By that formless [Brahman], its own form was fashioned by its own play, / endowed with all divine powers and qualities, full of all knowledge, auspicious,

2.1.s:
sarvagā sarvarūpā ca sarvadṛksarvakāriṇī |
sarvaikavandyā sarvādyā sarvadā sarvasaṃskṛtiḥ ||
2.1.d:
सर्वगा सर्वरूपा च सर्वदृक्सर्वकारिणी ।
सर्वैकवन्द्या सर्वाद्या सर्वदा सर्वसंस्कृतिः ॥
2.1.m: all-pervading, all-formed, all-seeing, the maker of all, / the sole one praised by all, the origin of all, always bringing perfection to all.

2.1.s:
parikalpyeti tāṃ mūrtimaiśvarīṃ śuddharūpiṇīm |
advitīyamanādyantaṃ sarvābhāsaṃ cidātmakam |
antardadhe parākhyaṃ yad brahma sarvagamavyayam ||
2.1.d:
परिकल्प्येति तां मूर्तिमैश्वरीं शुद्धरूपिणीम् ।
अद्वितीयमनाद्यन्तं सर्वाभासं चिदात्मकम् ।
अन्तर्दधे पराख्यं यद् ब्रह्म सर्वगमव्ययम् ॥
2.1.m: Having thus fashioned that divine form of pure nature, / without a second, without beginning or end, the illuminator of all, consisting of consciousness, / that all-pervading, imperishable Brahman, called the supreme, concealed itself.

2.1.s:
amūrte yatparākhyaṃ vai tasya mūrtiḥ sadāśivaḥ |
arvācīnāḥ parācīnā īśvaraṃ taṃ jagurbudhāḥ ||
2.1.d:
अमूर्ते यत्पराख्यं वै तस्य मूर्तिः सदाशिवः ।
अर्वाचीनाः पराचीना ईश्वरं तं जगुर्बुधाः ॥
2.1.m: Of that formless reality called the supreme, the form is Sadāśiva; / the wise of earlier and later times have proclaimed him to be Īśvara.

2.1.s:
śaktistadaikalenāpi svairaṃ viharatā tanuḥ |
svavigrahātsvayaṃ sṛṣṭā svaśarīrānapāyinī ||
2.1.d:
शक्तिस्तदैकलेनापि स्वैरं विहरता तनुः ।
स्वविग्रहात्स्वयं सृष्टा स्वशरीरानपायिनी ॥
2.1.m: Then a power, a bodily form, wandering freely at will, / was created by him from his own body through himself alone, never departing from his own body.

2.1.s:
pradhānaṃ prakṛtiṃ tāṃ ca māyāṃ guṇavatīṃ parām |
buddhitattvasya jananīmāhurvikṛtivarjitām ||
2.1.d:
प्रधानं प्रकृतिं तां च मायां गुणवतीं पराम् ।
बुद्धितत्त्वस्य जननीमाहुर्विकृतिवर्जिताम् ॥
2.1.m: That they call Pradhāna, Prakṛti, the supreme Māyā endowed with the qualities, / the mother of the intellect-principle, free from transformation.

2.1.s:
sā śaktirambikā proktā prakṛtiḥ sakaleśvarī |
tridevajananī nityā mūlakāraṇamityuta ||
2.1.d:
सा शक्तिरम्बिका प्रोक्ता प्रकृतिः सकलेश्वरी ।
त्रिदेवजननी नित्या मूलकारणमित्युत ॥
2.1.m: That power is called Ambikā, Prakṛti, the mistress of all, / the eternal mother of the three gods, and indeed the root cause.

2.1.s:
asyā aṣṭau bhujāścāsanvicitravadanā śubhā |
rākācandrasahasrasya vadane bhāśca nityaśaḥ ||
2.1.d:
अस्या अष्टौ भुजाश्चासन्विचित्रवदना शुभा ।
राकाचन्द्रसहस्रस्य वदने भाश्च नित्यशः ॥
2.1.m: She had eight arms, a wondrous face, auspicious, / and in her face was always the radiance of a thousand full moons.

2.1.s:
nānābharaṇasaṃyuktā nānāgatisamanvitā |
nānāyudhadharā devī phullapaṅkajalocanā ||
2.1.d:
नानाभरणसंयुक्ता नानागतिसमन्विता ।
नानायुधधरा देवी फुल्लपङ्कजलोचना ॥
2.1.m: Adorned with various ornaments, endowed with varied movements, / the goddess bore various weapons, her eyes like blooming lotuses.

2.1.s:
acintyatejasā yuktā sarvayoniḥ samudyatā |
ekākinī yadā māyā saṃyogāccāpyanekikā ||
2.1.d:
अचिन्त्यतेजसा युक्ता सर्वयोनिः समुद्यता ।
एकाकिनी यदा माया संयोगाच्चाप्यनेकिका ॥
2.1.m: Endowed with inconceivable splendour, the source of all, energetic, / when she is alone she is Māyā, and through union she is multiform.

2.1.s:
paraḥ pumānīśvaraḥ sa śivaḥ śambhuranīśvaraḥ |
śīrṣe mandākinīdhārī bhālacandrastrilocanaḥ ||
2.1.d:
परः पुमानीश्वरः स शिवः शम्भुरनीश्वरः ।
शीर्षे मन्दाकिनीधारी भालचन्द्रस्त्रिलोचनः ॥
2.1.m: The supreme Person, Īśvara, is Śiva, Śambhu, who has no master; / he bears the Mandākinī on his head, with a crescent moon on his forehead and three eyes.

2.1.s:
pañcavaktraḥ prasannātmā daśabāhustriśūladhṛk |
karpūragaurasusito bhasmoddhūlitavigrahaḥ ||
2.1.d:
पञ्चवक्त्रः प्रसन्नात्मा दशबाहुस्त्रिशूलधृक् ।
कर्पूरगौरसुसितो भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहः ॥
2.1.m: Five-faced, peaceful in spirit, ten-armed, wielding a trident, / white as camphor, pure white, his body smeared with ashes.

2.1.s:
yugapacca tayā śaktyā sākaṃ kālasvarūpiṇā |
śivalokābhidhaṃ kṣetraṃ nirmitaṃ tena brahmaṇā ||
2.1.d:
युगपच्च तया शक्त्या साकं कालस्वरूपिणा ।
शिवलोकाभिधं क्षेत्रं निर्मितं तेन ब्रह्मणा ॥
2.1.m: Simultaneously, together with that power, in the form of Time, / that Brahman fashioned the sacred site called Śivaloka.

2.1.s:
tadeva kāśiketyetatprocyate kṣetramuttamam |
paraṃ nirvāṇasaṅkhyānaṃ sarvopari virājitam ||
2.1.d:
तदेव काशिकेत्येतत्प्रोच्यते क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ।
परं निर्वाणसङ्ख्यानं सर्वोपरि विराजितम् ॥
2.1.m: That very excellent sacred site is called Kāśikā, / the highest place designated for liberation, reigning supreme above all.

2.1.s:
tābhyāṃ ca ramamāṇābhyāṃ tasminkṣetre manorame |
paramānandarūpābhyāṃ paramānandarūpiṇam ||
2.1.d:
ताभ्यां च रममाणाभ्यां तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे मनोरमे ।
परमानन्दरूपाभ्यां परमानन्दरूपिणम् ॥
2.1.m: And by those two taking delight in that delightful sacred site, / having the nature of supreme bliss, [the site] of the nature of supreme bliss—

2.1.s:
mune pralayakāle'pi na tatkṣetraṃ kadācana |
vimuktaṃ hi śivābhyāṃ yadavimuktaṃ tato viduḥ ||
2.1.d:
मुने प्रलयकालेऽपि न तत्क्षेत्रं कदाचन ।
विमुक्तं हि शिवाभ्यां यदविमुक्तं ततो विदुः ॥
2.1.m: O sage, even at the time of dissolution that sacred site was never / abandoned by Śiva and Śivā; therefore they know it as Avimukta.

2.1.s:
asyānandavanaṃ nāma purākāri pinākinā |
kṣetrasyānandahetutvādavimuktamanantaram ||
2.1.d:
अस्यानन्दवनं नाम पुराकारि पिनाकिना ।
क्षेत्रस्यानन्दहेतुत्वादविमुक्तमनन्तरम् ॥
2.1.m: Its name was made Ānandavana formerly by Pinākin, / because that sacred site was the cause of joy, and subsequently Avimukta.

2.1.s:
athānandavane tasmin śivayo ramamāṇayoḥ |
icchetyabhūtsurarṣe hi sṛjyaḥ ko'pyaparaḥ kila ||
2.1.d:
अथानन्दवने तस्मिन् शिवयो रममाणयोः ।
इच्छेत्यभूत्सुरर्षे हि सृज्यः कोऽप्यपरः किल ॥
2.1.m: Then, in that Ānandavana, as the two Śivas took their delight, / this wish arose, O divine sage: "Indeed, let someone else be created,

2.1.s:
yasmin nyasya mahābhāramāvāṃ svasvairacāriṇau |
nirvāṇadhāraṇaṃ kurvaḥ kevalaṃ kāśiśāyinau ||
2.1.d:
यस्मिन् न्यस्य महाभारमावां स्वस्वैरचारिणौ ।
निर्वाणधारणं कुर्वः केवलं काशिशायिनौ ॥
2.1.m: upon whom having placed this great burden, we two, wandering at our own will, / may maintain liberation alone, resting in Kāśī.

2.1.s:
sa eva sarvaṃ kurutāṃ sa eva paripātu ca |
sa eva saṃvṛṇotvante madanugrahataḥsadā ||
2.1.d:
स एव सर्वं कुरुतां स एव परिपातु च ।
स एव संवृणोत्वन्ते मदनुग्रहतःसदा ॥
2.1.m: Let him alone do everything, let him alone protect [all], / let him alone gather up [all] at the end, constantly through my grace.

2.1.s:
cetaḥ samudramākuñcya cintākallolalolitam |
sattvaratnaṃ tamogrāhaṃ rajovidrumavallitam ||
2.1.d:
चेतः समुद्रमाकुञ्च्य चिन्ताकल्लोललोलितम् ।
सत्त्वरत्नं तमोग्राहं रजोविद्रुमवल्लितम् ॥
2.1.m: Restraining the ocean of the mind agitated by the waves of thought, / having the jewel of sattva, the sea-monster of tamas, and the coral vine of rajas,

2.1.s:
yasya prasādāttiṣṭhāvaḥ sukhamānandakānane |
parikṣiptamanovṛttau bahiścintāture sukham ||
2.1.d:
यस्य प्रसादात्तिष्ठावः सुखमानन्दकानने ।
परिक्षिप्तमनोवृत्तौ बहिश्चिन्तातुरे सुखम् ॥
2.1.m: by whose grace we two may abide happily in Ānandakānana, / while the activity of mind is cast aside, free from concern about the outside world."

2.1.s:
sampradhāryeti sa vibhustayā śaktyā pareśvaraḥ |
savye vyāpārayāñcakre daśame'ṅge sudhāsavam ||
2.1.d:
सम्प्रधार्येति स विभुस्तया शक्त्या परेश्वरः ।
सव्ये व्यापारयाञ्चक्रे दशमेऽङ्गे सुधासवम् ॥
2.1.m: Having resolved thus, that all-pervading lord, the supreme ruler, with that power, / set in motion the nectar of immortality upon his tenth limb, the left.

2.1.s:
tataḥ pumānāvirāsīdekastrailokyasundaraḥ |
śāntaḥsattvaguṇodrikto gāmbhīryāmitasāgaraḥ ||
2.1.d:
ततः पुमानाविरासीदेकस्त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरः ।
शान्तःसत्त्वगुणोद्रिक्तो गाम्भीर्यामितसागरः ॥
2.1.m: From it a person appeared, the single most handsome in the three worlds, / tranquil, overflowing with the quality of sattva, an boundless ocean of profundity,

2.1.s:
tathā ca kṣamayā yukto mune'labdhopamo'bhavat |
indranīladyutiḥ śrīmānpuṇḍarīkottamekṣaṇaḥ ||
2.1.d:
तथा च क्षमया युक्तो मुनेऽलब्धोपमोऽभवत् ।
इन्द्रनीलद्युतिः श्रीमान्पुण्डरीकोत्तमेक्षणः ॥
2.1.m: and endowed with such patience, O sage, that he had no equal, / with the lustre of a sapphire, glorious, with eyes like the finest lotuses,

2.1.s:
suvarṇakāntibhṛcchreṣṭhadukūlayugalāvṛtaḥ |
lasatpracaṇḍadordaṇḍayugalo hyaparājitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
सुवर्णकान्तिभृच्छ्रेष्ठदुकूलयुगलावृतः ।
लसत्प्रचण्डदोर्दण्डयुगलो ह्यपराजितः ॥
2.1.m: clad in a pair of excellent silken garments bearing the radiance of gold, / with a pair of splendid, mighty arms, unconquered.

2.1.s:
tataḥ sa puruṣaḥ śambhuṃ praṇamya parameśvaram |
nāmāni kuru me svāminvada karma jagāvati ||
2.1.d:
ततः स पुरुषः शम्भुं प्रणम्य परमेश्वरम् ।
नामानि कुरु मे स्वामिन्वद कर्म जगावति ॥
2.1.m: Then that person, having bowed to Śambhu, the supreme lord, said: / "O Master, give me names, and declare my task in protecting the world."

2.1.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ prāha śaṅkaraḥ prahasanprabhuḥ |
puruṣaṃ taṃ maheśāno vācā meghagabhīrayā ||
2.1.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं प्राह शङ्करः प्रहसन्प्रभुः ।
पुरुषं तं महेशानो वाचा मेघगभीरया ॥
2.1.m: Hearing that speech, the lord Śaṅkara, Maheśāna, smiling, / addressed that person in a voice deep as a thundercloud.

2.1.s:
śiva uvāca |
viṣṇviti vyāpakatvātte nāma khyātaṃ bhaviṣyati |
bahūnyanyāni nāmāni bhaktasaukhyakarāṇi ha ||
2.1.d:
शिव उवाच ।
विष्ण्विति व्यापकत्वात्ते नाम ख्यातं भविष्यति ।
बहून्यन्यानि नामानि भक्तसौख्यकराणि ह ॥
2.1.m: Śiva said: / "Because of your pervasiveness your name shall be renowned as Viṣṇu, / and you will have many other names that bring joy to devotees.

2.1.s:
tapaḥ kuru dṛḍho bhūtvā paramaṃ kāryasādhanam |
ityuktvā śvāsamārgeṇa dadau ca nigamaṃ tataḥ ||
2.1.d:
तपः कुरु दृढो भूत्वा परमं कार्यसाधनम् ।
इत्युक्त्वा श्वासमार्गेण ददौ च निगमं ततः ॥
2.1.m: Perform austerity, becoming steadfast, for the supreme accomplishment of your task." / Having spoken thus, through the pathway of his breath he then imparted the Veda.

2.1.s:
tato'cyutaḥ śivaṃ natvā cakāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ |
antardhānaṃ gataḥ śaktyā salokaḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
2.1.d:
ततोऽच्युतः शिवं नत्वा चकार विपुलं तपः ।
अन्तर्धानं गतः शक्त्या सलोकः परमेश्वरः ॥
2.1.m: Then Acyuta, having bowed to Śiva, performed extensive austerity; / the supreme lord with his power and his realm disappeared from sight.

2.1.s:
divyaṃ dvādaśasāhasraṃ varṣaṃ taptvāpi cācyutaḥ |
na prāpa svābhilaṣitaṃ sarvadaṃ śambhudarśanam ||
2.1.d:
दिव्यं द्वादशसाहस्रं वर्षं तप्त्वापि चाच्युतः ।
न प्राप स्वाभिलषितं सर्वदं शम्भुदर्शनम् ॥
2.1.m: Even having performed austerity for twelve thousand divine years, Acyuta / did not obtain the desired sight of Śambhu, the bestower of all.

2.1.s:
tataḥ saṃśayamāpannaścintitaṃ hṛdi sādaram |
mayādya kiṃ prakartavyamiti viṣṇuḥ śivaṃ smaran ||
2.1.d:
ततः संशयमापन्नश्चिन्तितं हृदि सादरम् ।
मयाद्य किं प्रकर्तव्यमिति विष्णुः शिवं स्मरन् ॥
2.1.m: Then, fallen into doubt, Viṣṇu, remembering Śiva, / considered respectfully in his heart: "What is to be done by me now?"

2.1.s:
etasminnantare vāṇī samutpannā śivācchubhā |
tapaḥ punaḥ prakartavyaṃ saṃśayasyāpanuttaye ||
2.1.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वाणी समुत्पन्ना शिवाच्छुभा ।
तपः पुनः प्रकर्तव्यं संशयस्यापनुत्तये ॥
2.1.m: At that moment, an auspicious voice arose from Śiva: / "Austerity must be performed again, for the dispelling of doubt."

2.1.s:
tatastena ca tacchrutvā tapastaptaṃ sudāruṇam |
bahukālaṃ tadā brahmadhyānamārgapareṇa hi ||
2.1.d:
ततस्तेन च तच्छ्रुत्वा तपस्तप्तं सुदारुणम् ।
बहुकालं तदा ब्रह्मध्यानमार्गपरेण हि ॥
2.1.m: Then, having heard that, he performed severe austerity / for a long time, intent on the path of meditation on Brahman.

2.1.s:
tataḥ sa puruṣo viṣṇuḥ prabuddho dhyānamārgataḥ |
suprīto vismayaṃ prāptaḥ kiṃ yattattavamaho iti ||
2.1.d:
ततः स पुरुषो विष्णुः प्रबुद्धो ध्यानमार्गतः ।
सुप्रीतो विस्मयं प्राप्तः किं यत्तत्तवमहो इति ॥
2.1.m: Then that Puruṣa, Viṣṇu, awakened from the path of meditation, / was greatly delighted and filled with wonder: “Oh, what is that principle?”

2.1.s:
pariśramavatastasya viṣṇoḥ svāṅgebhya eva ca |
jaladhārā hi saṃyātā vividhāḥ śivamāyayā ||
2.1.d:
परिश्रमवतस्तस्य विष्णोः स्वाङ्गेभ्य एव च ।
जलधारा हि संयाता विविधाः शिवमायया ॥
2.1.m: From the very limbs of that weary Viṣṇu, / various streams of water issued forth by the māyā of Śiva.

2.1.s:
abhivyāptaṃ ca sakalaṃ śūnyaṃ yattanmahāmune |
brahmarūpaṃ jalamabhūtsparśanātpāpanāśanam ||
2.1.d:
अभिव्याप्तं च सकलं शून्यं यत्तन्महामुने ।
ब्रह्मरूपं जलमभूत्स्पर्शनात्पापनाशनम् ॥
2.1.m: And whatever was empty was pervaded [by them], O great sage. / The water took the form of Brahman, destroying sin by its touch.

2.1.s:
tadā śrāntaśca puruṣo viṣṇustasmiñjale svayam |
suṣvāpa paramaprīto bahukālaṃ vimohitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
तदा श्रान्तश्च पुरुषो विष्णुस्तस्मिञ्जले स्वयम् ।
सुष्वाप परमप्रीतो बहुकालं विमोहितः ॥
2.1.m: Then the weary Puruṣa, Viṣṇu, himself slept in that water / for a long time, deeply delighted, bewildered [by māyā].

2.1.s:
nārāyaṇeti nāmāpi tasyāsīcchrutisammatam |
nānyatkiñcittadā hyāsītprākṛtaṃ puruṣaṃ vinā ||
2.1.d:
नारायणेति नामापि तस्यासीच्छ्रुतिसम्मतम् ।
नान्यत्किञ्चित्तदा ह्यासीत्प्राकृतं पुरुषं विना ॥
2.1.m: His name, confirmed by the scriptures, was Nārāyaṇa; / at that time there was nothing else, apart from the material Puruṣa.

2.1.s:
etasminnantare kāle tattvānyāsanmahātmanaḥ |
tatprakāraṃ śṛṇu prājña gadato me mahāmate ||
2.1.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे काले तत्त्वान्यासन्महात्मनः ।
तत्प्रकारं शृणु प्राज्ञ गदतो मे महामते ॥
2.1.m: In that intervening time, the principles of the great-souled one arose. / Hear their manner, O wise one of great intellect, as I tell it.

2.1.s:
prakṛteśca mahānāsīnmahataśca guṇāstrayaḥ |
ahaṅkārastato jātastrividho guṇabhedataḥ ||
2.1.d:
प्रकृतेश्च महानासीन्महतश्च गुणास्त्रयः ।
अहङ्कारस्ततो जातस्त्रिविधो गुणभेदतः ॥
2.1.m: From Prakṛti came Mahat, and from Mahat the three guṇas. / From that arose ahaṅkāra, threefold according to the division of the guṇas.

2.1.s:
tanmātraśca tato jātāḥ pañca bhūtāni vai tataḥ |
tadaiva tānīndriyāṇi jñānakarmamayāni ca ||
2.1.d:
तन्मात्रश्च ततो जाताः पञ्च भूतानि वै ततः ।
तदैव तानीन्द्रियाणि ज्ञानकर्ममयानि च ॥
2.1.m: From that arose the subtle elements, and from them the five gross elements; / at that very time arose those sense faculties composed of knowledge and action.

2.1.s:
tattvānāmiti saṅkhyānamuktaṃ te ṛṣisattama |
jaḍātmakaṃ ca tatsarvaṃ prakṛteḥ puruṣaṃ vinā ||
2.1.d:
तत्त्वानामिति सङ्ख्यानमुक्तं ते ऋषिसत्तम ।
जडात्मकं च तत्सर्वं प्रकृतेः पुरुषं विना ॥
2.1.m: Thus the enumeration of the principles has been spoken to you, O best of sages; / and all of that is inanimate, arising from Prakṛti, apart from the Puruṣa.

2.1.s:
tattadaikīkṛtaṃ tattvaṃ caturviṃśatisaṅkhyakam |
śivecchayā gṛhītvā sa suṣvāpa brahmarūpake ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaḥ sṛṣṭikhaṇḍeḥ
2.1.d:
तत्तदैकीकृतं तत्त्वं चतुर्विंशतिसङ्ख्यकम् ।
शिवेच्छया गृहीत्वा स सुष्वाप ब्रह्मरूपके ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां प्रथमः सृष्टिखण्डेः
2.1.m:
Uniting those principles, twenty-four in number, / he took them by the will of Śiva and slept in [that water] which had the form of Brahman.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled “The Description of the Origin of Viṣṇu,” in the explanation of creation in the first section of the second Rudrasaṃhitā of the illustrious Śivapurāṇa.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
supte nārāyaṇe deve nābhau paṅkajamuttamam |
āvirbabhūva sahasā bṛhadvai śaṅkarecchayā ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
सुप्ते नारायणे देवे नाभौ पङ्कजमुत्तमम् ।
आविर्बभूव सहसा बृहद्वै शङ्करेच्छया ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / When the god Nārāyaṇa had fallen asleep, an excellent, vast lotus / suddenly appeared in his navel by the will of Śaṅkara.

2.1.s:
anantayaṣṭikāyuktaṃ karṇikārasamaprabham |
anantayojanāyāmamanantocchrāyasaṃyutam ||
2.1.d:
अनन्तयष्टिकायुक्तं कर्णिकारसमप्रभम् ।
अनन्तयोजनायाममनन्तोच्छ्रायसंयुतम् ॥
2.1.m: Endowed with countless stalks, having a splendor like the Karṇikāra flower, / stretching for countless leagues and endowed with boundless height,

2.1.s:
koṭisūryapratīkāśaṃ sundaraṃ tattvasaṃyutam |
atyadbhutaṃ mahāramyaṃ darśanīyamanuttamam ||
2.1.d:
कोटिसूर्यप्रतीकाशं सुन्दरं तत्त्वसंयुतम् ।
अत्यद्भुतं महारम्यं दर्शनीयमनुत्तमम् ॥
2.1.m: resembling ten million suns, beautiful, containing the principles, / most wonderful, exceedingly charming, lovely to behold, unsurpassed.

2.1.s:
kṛtvā yatnaṃ pūrvavatsa śaṅkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ |
dakṣiṇāṅgānnijānmāṃ vai sāmbaḥ śambhurajījanat ||
2.1.d:
कृत्वा यत्नं पूर्ववत्स शङ्करः परमेश्वरः ।
दक्षिणाङ्गान्निजान्मां वै साम्बः शम्भुरजीजनत् ॥
2.1.m: Making an effort as before, Parameśvara Śaṅkara, / Śambhu accompanied by Ambā, produced me from his right side.

2.1.s:
sa māyāmohitaṃ kṛtvā māṃ maheśo drutaṃ mune |
tannābhipaṅkajādāvirbhāvayāmāsa līlayā ||
2.1.d:
स मायामोहितं कृत्वा मां महेशो द्रुतं मुने ।
तन्नाभिपङ्कजादाविर्भावयामास लीलया ॥
2.1.m: Having deluded me with his māyā, Maheśa quickly, O sage, / manifested me in sport from the navel-lotus of that [Viṣṇu].

2.1.s:
evaṃ padmāttato jajñe putro'haṃ hemagarbhakaḥ |
caturmukho raktavarṇastripuṇḍrāṅkitamastakaḥ ||
2.1.d:
एवं पद्मात्ततो जज्ञे पुत्रोऽहं हेमगर्भकः ।
चतुर्मुखो रक्तवर्णस्त्रिपुण्ड्राङ्कितमस्तकः ॥
2.1.m: Thus from that lotus I was born as a son, having a golden womb, / four-faced, red in complexion, with a head marked by the tripuṇḍra.

2.1.s:
tanmāyāmohitaścāhaṃ nāvidaṃ kamalaṃ vinā |
svadehajanakaṃ tāta pitaraṃ jñānadurbalaḥ ||
2.1.d:
तन्मायामोहितश्चाहं नाविदं कमलं विना ।
स्वदेहजनकं तात पितरं ज्ञानदुर्बलः ॥
2.1.m: Deluded by his māyā, I did not know anyone apart from the lotus, / weak in understanding, [ignorant of] the father who produced my own body, O dear one.

2.1.s:
ko'haṃ vā kuta āyātaḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ tu madīyakam |
kasya putro'hamutpannaḥ kenaiva nirmito'dhunā ||
2.1.d:
कोऽहं वा कुत आयातः किं कार्यं तु मदीयकम् ।
कस्य पुत्रोऽहमुत्पन्नः केनैव निर्मितोऽधुना ॥
2.1.m: “Who am I? Or whence have I come? What is my task? / Whose son am I born? By whom have I now been made?”

2.1.s:
iti saṃśayamāpannaṃ buddhirmāṃ samapadyata |
kimarthaṃ mohamāyāmi tajjñānaṃ sukaraṃ khalu ||
2.1.d:
इति संशयमापन्नं बुद्धिर्मां समपद्यत ।
किमर्थं मोहमायामि तज्ज्ञानं सुकरं खलु ॥
2.1.m: As I was filled with doubt, the thought occurred to me: / “Why do I fall into delusion? Knowledge of that is surely easy to attain.

2.1.s:
etatkamalapuṣpasya patrārohasthalaṃ hyadhaḥ |
matkartā ca sa vai tatra bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.1.d:
एतत्कमलपुष्पस्य पत्रारोहस्थलं ह्यधः ।
मत्कर्ता च स वै तत्र भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
2.1.m: The place where the petals of this lotus flower rise up is down below; / and my maker will surely be there, no doubt.”

2.1.s:
na labdhaṃ tu mayā tatra kamalasthānamuttamam |
saṃśayaṃ ca punaḥ prāptaḥ kamale gantumutsukaḥ ||
2.1.d:
न लब्धं तु मया तत्र कमलस्थानमुत्तमम् ।
संशयं च पुनः प्राप्तः कमले गन्तुमुत्सुकः ॥
2.1.m: Yet I did not find that excellent base of the lotus; / and fallen into doubt again, I became eager to go back to the lotus.

2.1.s:
ārurohātha kamalaṃ nālamārgeṇa vai mune |
kuḍmalaṃ kamalasyātha labdhavānna vimohitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
आरुरोहाथ कमलं नालमार्गेण वै मुने ।
कुड्मलं कमलस्याथ लब्धवान्न विमोहितः ॥
2.1.m: Then I climbed up the lotus along the path of the stalk, O sage; / yet bewildered, I did not find the bud of the lotus.

2.1.s:
nālamārgeṇa bhramato gataṃ varṣaśataṃ punaḥ |
kṣaṇamātraṃ tadā tatra tatastiṣṭhanvimohitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
नालमार्गेण भ्रमतो गतं वर्षशतं पुनः ।
क्षणमात्रं तदा तत्र ततस्तिष्ठन्विमोहितः ॥
2.1.m: Another hundred years passed as I wandered along the path of the stalk; / then, standing there for a mere moment, I was utterly bewildered.

2.1.s:
tadā vāṇī samutpannā tapeti paramā śubhā |
śivecchayā parā vyomno mohavidhvaṃsinī mune ||
2.1.d:
तदा वाणी समुत्पन्ना तपेति परमा शुभा ।
शिवेच्छया परा व्योम्नो मोहविध्वंसिनी मुने ॥
2.1.m: Then from the sky arose a supreme, auspicious voice saying “Perform austerity,” / supreme, destroying delusion by the will of Śiva, O sage.

2.1.s:
tacchrutvā vyomavacanaṃ dvādaśābdaṃ prayatnataḥ |
punastaptaṃ tapo ghoraṃ draṣṭuṃ svajanakaṃ tadā ||
2.1.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा व्योमवचनं द्वादशाब्दं प्रयत्नतः ।
पुनस्तप्तं तपो घोरं द्रष्टुं स्वजनकं तदा ॥
2.1.m: Hearing that speech from the sky, I then diligently / performed dreadful austerity again for twelve years in order to see my progenitor.

2.1.s:
tadā hi bhagavānviṣṇuścaturbāhuḥ sulocanaḥ |
mayyevānugrahaṃ kartuṃ drutamāvirbabhūva ha ||
2.1.d:
तदा हि भगवान्विष्णुश्चतुर्बाहुः सुलोचनः ।
मय्येवानुग्रहं कर्तुं द्रुतमाविर्बभूव ह ॥
2.1.m: Then the blessed lord Viṣṇu, four-armed and beautiful-eyed, / suddenly appeared in order to show favor to me.

2.1.s:
śaṅkhacakrāyudhakaro gadāpadmadharaḥ paraḥ |
ghanaśyāmalasarvāṅgaḥ pītāmbaradharaḥ paraḥ ||
2.1.d:
शङ्खचक्रायुधकरो गदापद्मधरः परः ।
घनश्यामलसर्वाङ्गः पीताम्बरधरः परः ॥
2.1.m: Bearing the conch and discus as weapons in his hands, holding a mace and a lotus, / his whole body dark as a raincloud, clad in yellow garments, supreme,

2.1.s:
mukuṭādimahābhūṣaḥ prasannamukhapaṅkajaḥ |
koṭikandarpasaṅkāśaḥsandṛṣṭo mohitena saḥ ||
2.1.d:
मुकुटादिमहाभूषः प्रसन्नमुखपङ्कजः ।
कोटिकन्दर्पसङ्काशःसन्दृष्टो मोहितेन सः ॥
2.1.m: adorned with great ornaments such as a crown, with a cheerful lotus-like face, / resembling ten million gods of love—he was beheld by me who was deluded.

2.1.s:
tad dṛṣṭvā sundaraṃ rūpaṃ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ |
kālābhaṃ kāñcanābhaṃ ca sarvātmānaṃ caturbhujam ||
2.1.d:
तद् दृष्ट्वा सुन्दरं रूपं विस्मयं परमं गतः ।
कालाभं काञ्चनाभं च सर्वात्मानं चतुर्भुजम् ॥
2.1.m: Beholding that beautiful form, I was filled with the highest wonder— / him possessing the hue of a dark cloud and the hue of gold, the Self of all, four-armed.

2.1.s:
tathābhūtamahaṃ dṛṣṭvā sadasanmayamātmanā |
nārāyaṇaṃ mahābāhuṃ harṣito hyabhavaṃ tadā ||
2.1.d:
तथाभूतमहं दृष्ट्वा सदसन्मयमात्मना ।
नारायणं महाबाहुं हर्षितो ह्यभवं तदा ॥
2.1.m: Seeing Nārāyaṇa of mighty arms, who had thus become / the real and the unreal within himself, I then became joyful.

2.1.s:
māyayā mohitaḥ śambhostadā līlātmanaḥ prabhoḥ |
avijñāya svajanakaṃ tamavocaṃ praharṣitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
मायया मोहितः शम्भोस्तदा लीलात्मनः प्रभोः ।
अविज्ञाय स्वजनकं तमवोचं प्रहर्षितः ॥
2.1.m: Deluded by the māyā of Śambhu, the lord whose nature is sport, / not recognizing my own father, I spoke to him in delight.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
kastvaṃ vadeti hastena samutthāpya sanātanam |
tadā hastaprahāreṇa tīvreṇa sudṛḍhena tu ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
कस्त्वं वदेति हस्तेन समुत्थाप्य सनातनम् ।
तदा हस्तप्रहारेण तीव्रेण सुदृढेन तु ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / “Say, who are you?” raising the eternal one with my hand, / at that time with a sharp, forceful blow of my hand.

2.1.s:
prabuddhyotthāya śayanātsamāsīnaḥ kṣaṇaṃ vaśī |
dadarśa nidrāviklinna nīrajāmalalocanaḥ ||
2.1.d:
प्रबुद्ध्योत्थाय शयनात्समासीनः क्षणं वशी ।
ददर्श निद्राविक्लिन्न नीरजामललोचनः ॥
2.1.m: Awakening and rising from his bed, the self-controlled one sat for a moment / and looked, his spotless lotus-eyes moist with sleep.

2.1.s:
māmatra saṃsthitaṃ bhāsādhyāsito bhagavānhariḥ |
āha cotthāya brahmāṇaṃ hasanmāṃ madhuraṃ sakṛt ||
2.1.d:
मामत्र संस्थितं भासाध्यासितो भगवान्हरिः ।
आह चोत्थाय ब्रह्माणं हसन्मां मधुरं सकृत् ॥
2.1.m: The blessed lord Hari, seated there in radiant splendor, / rose and, smiling gently once, spoke to me, Brahmā:

2.1.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
svāgataṃ svāgataṃ vatsa pitāmaha mahādyute |
nirbhayo bhava dāsye'haṃ sarvānkāmānna saṃśayaḥ ||
2.1.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
स्वागतं स्वागतं वत्स पितामह महाद्युते ।
निर्भयो भव दास्येऽहं सर्वान्कामान्न संशयः ॥
2.1.m: Viṣṇu said: / “Welcome, welcome, my child, Grandfather of great splendor! / Be fearless; I shall grant you all desires, no doubt.”

2.1.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā smitapūrvaṃ surarṣabhaḥ |
rajasā baddhavairaśca tamavocaṃ janārdanam ||
2.1.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा स्मितपूर्वं सुरर्षभः ।
रजसा बद्धवैरश्च तमवोचं जनार्दनम् ॥
2.1.m: Hearing those words of his accompanied by a smile, I, the best of the gods, / seized with enmity through the quality of rajas, spoke to that Janārdana:

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
bhāṣase vatsa vatseti sarvasaṃhārakāraṇam |
māmihāti smitaṃ kṛtvā guruḥ śiṣyamivānagha ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
भाषसे वत्स वत्सेति सर्वसंहारकारणम् ।
मामिहाति स्मितं कृत्वा गुरुः शिष्यमिवानघ ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / “You speak to me, saying ‘Child, child,’ smiling excessively here / like a teacher to a pupil, O sinless one, to me who am the cause of universal dissolution,

2.1.s:
kartāraṃ jagatāṃ sākṣātprakṛteśca pravartakam |
sanātanamajaṃ viṣṇuṃ viriñciṃ viṣṇusambhavam ||
2.1.d:
कर्तारं जगतां साक्षात्प्रकृतेश्च प्रवर्तकम् ।
सनातनमजं विष्णुं विरिञ्चिं विष्णुसम्भवम् ॥
2.1.m: the direct creator of the worlds, the impeller of Prakṛti, / the eternal, unborn Viṣṇu, Viriñci, born of Viṣṇu,

2.1.s:
viśvātmānaṃ vidhātāraṃ dhātāraṃ paṅkajekṣaṇam |
kimarthaṃ bhāṣase mohādvaktumarhasi satvaram ||
2.1.d:
विश्वात्मानं विधातारं धातारं पङ्कजेक्षणम् ।
किमर्थं भाषसे मोहाद्वक्तुमर्हसि सत्वरम् ॥
2.1.m: the Self of the universe, the ordainer, the supporter, lotus-eyed! / Why do you speak out of delusion? You should speak at once.

2.1.s:
vedo māṃ vakti niyamātsvayambhuvamajaṃ vibhum |
pitāmahaṃ svarājaṃ ca parameṣṭhinamuttamam ||
2.1.d:
वेदो मां वक्ति नियमात्स्वयम्भुवमजं विभुम् ।
पितामहं स्वराजं च परमेष्ठिनमुत्तमम् ॥
2.1.m: The Veda invariably declares me to be self-born, unborn, all-pervading, / the Grandfather, the self-ruler, and the supreme Parameṣṭhin.”

2.1.s:
ityākarṇya harirvākyaṃ mama kruddho ramāpatiḥ |
so'pi māmāha jāne tvāṃ kartāramiti lokataḥ ||
2.1.d:
इत्याकर्ण्य हरिर्वाक्यं मम क्रुद्धो रमापतिः ।
सोऽपि मामाह जाने त्वां कर्तारमिति लोकतः ॥
2.1.m: Hearing my words, Hari, the lord of Ramā, became angry; / he too spoke to me: “I know you to be the creator according to the world.

2.1.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
kartuṃ dhartuṃ bhavānaṅgādavatīrṇo mamāvyayāt |
vismṛto'si jagannāthaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam ||
2.1.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
कर्तुं धर्तुं भवानङ्गादवतीर्णो ममाव्ययात् ।
विस्मृतोऽसि जगन्नाथं नारायणमनामयम् ॥
2.1.m: Viṣṇu said: / You have descended from my imperishable body to create and sustain; / you have forgotten the Lord of the World, Nārāyaṇa, free from affliction,

2.1.s:
puruṣaṃ paramātmānaṃ puruhūtaṃ puruṣṭutam |
viṣṇumacyutamīśānaṃ viśvasya prabhavodbhavam ||
2.1.d:
पुरुषं परमात्मानं पुरुहूतं पुरुष्टुतम् ।
विष्णुमच्युतमीशानं विश्वस्य प्रभवोद्भवम् ॥
2.1.m: the Puruṣa, the Supreme Self, invoked by many, praised by many, / Viṣṇu, Acyuta, the ruler, the origin of the origin of the universe.”

2.1.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ mahābāhuṃ sarvavyāpakamīśvaram |
mannābhipadmatastvaṃ hi prasūto nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
2.1.d:
नारायणं महाबाहुं सर्वव्यापकमीश्वरम् ।
मन्नाभिपद्मतस्त्वं हि प्रसूतो नात्र संशयः ॥
2.1.m: [Know me as] Nārāyaṇa, the mighty-armed, all-pervading Lord. / For you were born from my navel-lotus; there is no doubt about this.

2.1.s:
tavāparādho nāstyatra tvayi māyākṛtaṃ mama |
śṛṇu satyaṃ caturvaktra sarvadeveśvaro hyaham ||
2.1.d:
तवापराधो नास्त्यत्र त्वयि मायाकृतं मम ।
शृणु सत्यं चतुर्वक्त्र सर्वदेवेश्वरो ह्यहम् ॥
2.1.m: There is no fault of yours in this; it was caused by my māyā upon you. / Hear the truth, O four-faced one: I indeed am the Lord of all gods.

2.1.s:
kartā hartā ca bhartā ca na mayāsti samo vibhuḥ |
ahameva paraṃ brahma paraṃ tattvaṃ pitāmaha ||
2.1.d:
कर्ता हर्ता च भर्ता च न मयास्ति समो विभुः ।
अहमेव परं ब्रह्म परं तत्त्वं पितामह ॥
2.1.m: I am the creator, the destroyer, and the maintainer; there is no all-pervading lord equal to me. / I alone am the supreme Brahman, the supreme reality, O grandfather.

2.1.s:
ahameva paraṃ jyotiḥ paramātmā tvahaṃ vibhuḥ |
adya dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ sarvaṃ jagatyasmiñcarācaram ||
2.1.d:
अहमेव परं ज्योतिः परमात्मा त्वहं विभुः ।
अद्य दृष्टं श्रुतं सर्वं जगत्यस्मिञ्चराचरम् ॥
2.1.m: I alone am the supreme light; I am the supreme Self, the all-pervading lord. / Whatever moving and unmoving thing is seen or heard in this world today,

2.1.s:
tattadviddhi caturvaktra sarvaṃ manmayamityatha |
mayā sṛṣṭaṃ purāvyaktaṃ caturviṃśatitattvakam ||
2.1.d:
तत्तद्विद्धि चतुर्वक्त्र सर्वं मन्मयमित्यथ ।
मया सृष्टं पुराव्यक्तं चतुर्विंशतितत्त्वकम् ॥
2.1.m: know each and every one, O four-faced one, to be made of me. / Formerly, I created the unmanifest consisting of twenty-four principles.

2.1.s:
nityaṃ teṣvaṇavo baddhāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ krodhabhayādayaḥ |
prabhāvācca bhavānaṅgānyanekānīha līlayā ||
2.1.d:
नित्यं तेष्वणवो बद्धाः सृष्टाः क्रोधभयादयः ।
प्रभावाच्च भवानङ्गान्यनेकानीह लीलया ॥
2.1.m: Constantly within them, subtle souls are bound; wrath, fear, and the rest were created, / and, through [my] power and in mere play, you, along with your many limbs, [were brought forth] here.

2.1.s:
sṛṣṭā buddhirmayā tasyāmahaṅkārastridhā tataḥ |
tanmātraṃ pañcakaṃ tasmānmano dehendriyāṇi ca ||
2.1.d:
सृष्टा बुद्धिर्मया तस्यामहङ्कारस्त्रिधा ततः ।
तन्मात्रं पञ्चकं तस्मान्मनो देहेन्द्रियाणि च ॥
2.1.m: Intellect was created by me; from it, threefold egoism arose; / from that, the group of five subtle elements, and mind, the body, and the sense-organs;

2.1.s:
ākāśādīni bhūtāni bhautikāni ca līlayā |
iti buddhvā prajānātha śaraṇaṃ vraja me vidhe ||
2.1.d:
आकाशादीनि भूतानि भौतिकानि च लीलया ।
इति बुद्ध्वा प्रजानाथ शरणं व्रज मे विधे ॥
2.1.m: and space and the other elements, as well as elemental things, in play. / Knowing this, O lord of creatures, O creator, take refuge in me.

2.1.s:
ahaṃ tvāṃ sarvaduḥkhebhyo rakṣiṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ |
brahmovāca |
iti śrutvā vacastasya brahmā krodhasamanvitaḥ |
ko vā tvamiti sambhartsyābruvaṃ māyāvimohitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
अहं त्वां सर्वदुःखेभ्यो रक्षिष्यामि न संशयः ।
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य ब्रह्मा क्रोधसमन्वितः ।
को वा त्वमिति सम्भर्त्स्याब्रुवं मायाविमोहितः ॥
2.1.m:
I shall protect you from all sufferings, without a doubt."
Brahmā said:
Hearing these words of his, Brahmā became filled with wrath. / Deluded by māyā, I scolded [him] and said, "Who indeed are you?

2.1.s:
kimarthaṃ bhāṣase bhūri bahvanarthakaraṃ vacaḥ |
neśvarastvaṃ paraṃ brahma kaścitkartā bhavettava ||
2.1.d:
किमर्थं भाषसे भूरि बह्वनर्थकरं वचः ।
नेश्वरस्त्वं परं ब्रह्म कश्चित्कर्ता भवेत्तव ॥
2.1.m: Why do you speak such verbose words that cause great mischief? / You are not the Lord, the supreme Brahman; there must be some creator of you!"

2.1.s:
māyayā mohitaścāhaṃ yuddhaṃ cakre sudāruṇam |
hariṇā tena vai sārdhaṃ śaṅkarasya mahāprabhoḥ ||
2.1.d:
मायया मोहितश्चाहं युद्धं चक्रे सुदारुणम् ।
हरिणा तेन वै सार्धं शङ्करस्य महाप्रभोः ॥
2.1.m: And deluded by the māyā of Śaṅkara, the great Lord, / I engaged in a very terrible fight with that Hari.

2.1.s:
evaṃ mama hareścāsītsaṅgaro romaharṣaṇaḥ |
pralayārṇavamadhye tu rajasā baddhavairayoḥ ||
2.1.d:
एवं मम हरेश्चासीत्सङ्गरो रोमहर्षणः ।
प्रलयार्णवमध्ये तु रजसा बद्धवैरयोः ॥
2.1.m: Thus between me and Hari, our enmity bound fast by passion, / a hair-raising battle took place in the midst of the ocean of dissolution.

2.1.s:
etasminnantare liṅgamabhavaccāvayoḥ puraḥ |
vivādaśamanārthaṃ hi prabodhārthaṃ tathāvayoḥ ||
2.1.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे लिङ्गमभवच्चावयोः पुरः ।
विवादशमनार्थं हि प्रबोधार्थं तथावयोः ॥
2.1.m: In the meantime, a Liṅga appeared before the two of us, / in order to pacify the dispute and enlighten us both.

2.1.s:
jvālāmālāsahasrāḍhyaṃ kālānalaśatopamam |
kṣayavṛddhivinirmuktamādimadhyāntavarjitam ||
2.1.d:
ज्वालामालासहस्राढ्यं कालानलशतोपमम् ।
क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्तमादिमध्यान्तवर्जितम् ॥
2.1.m: It was rich with thousands of wreaths of flames, resembling a hundred fires of cosmic dissolution, / free from decay and increase, devoid of beginning, middle, and end,

2.1.s:
anaupamyamanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ viśvasambhavam |
tasya jvālāsahasreṇa mohito bhagavānhariḥ ||
2.1.d:
अनौपम्यमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं विश्वसम्भवम् ।
तस्य ज्वालासहस्रेण मोहितो भगवान्हरिः ॥
2.1.m: peerless, indescribable, unmanifest, the source of the universe. / Deluded by its thousands of flames, the blessed Lord Hari,

2.1.s:
mohitaṃ cāha māmatra kimarthaṃ spardhase'dhunā |
āgatastu tṛtīyo'tra tiṣṭhatāṃ yuddhamāvayoḥ ||
2.1.d:
मोहितं चाह मामत्र किमर्थं स्पर्धसेऽधुना ।
आगतस्तु तृतीयोऽत्र तिष्ठतां युद्धमावयोः ॥
2.1.m: himself bewildered, said to me: "Why do you compete with me now? / A third has arrived here; let our battle cease.

2.1.s:
kuta evātra sambhūtaḥ parīkṣāvo'gnisambhavam |
adho gamiṣyāmyanalastambhasyānupamasya ca ||
2.1.d:
कुत एवात्र सम्भूतः परीक्षावोऽग्निसम्भवम् ।
अधो गमिष्याम्यनलस्तम्भस्यानुपमस्य च ॥
2.1.m: From where has this arisen here? Let us both examine this origin of fire. / I shall go downwards beneath this peerless pillar of fire

2.1.s:
parīkṣārthaṃ prajānātha tasya vai vāyuvegataḥ |
bhavānūrdhvaṃ prayatnena gantumarhati satvaram ||
2.1.d:
परीक्षार्थं प्रजानाथ तस्य वै वायुवेगतः ।
भवानूर्ध्वं प्रयत्नेन गन्तुमर्हति सत्वरम् ॥
2.1.m: to investigate it, O lord of creatures, with the speed of the wind. / You ought to go upwards with effort and with all haste."

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
evaṃ vyāhṛtya viśvātmā svarūpamakarottadā |
vārāhamahamapyāśu haṃsatvaṃ prāptavānmune ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवं व्याहृत्य विश्वात्मा स्वरूपमकरोत्तदा ।
वाराहमहमप्याशु हंसत्वं प्राप्तवान्मुने ॥
2.1.m:
Brahmā said:
Having spoken thus, the Soul of the universe then took on / the form of a boar; and I also quickly attained the state of a swan, O sage.

2.1.s:
tadāprabhṛti māmāhurhaṃsahaṃso virāḍiti |
haṃsa haṃseti yo brūyātsa haṃso'tha bhaviṣyati ||
2.1.d:
तदाप्रभृति मामाहुर्हंसहंसो विराडिति ।
हंस हंसेति यो ब्रूयात्स हंसोऽथ भविष्यति ॥
2.1.m: From that time forward, people call me Haṃsahaṃsa, the sovereign ruler. / Whoever says 'haṃsa haṃsa' will indeed become a swan.

2.1.s:
suśveto hyanalaprakhyo viśvataḥ pakṣasaṃyutaḥ |
mano'nilajavo bhūtvā gatordhvaṃ cordhvataḥ purā ||
2.1.d:
सुश्वेतो ह्यनलप्रख्यो विश्वतः पक्षसंयुतः ।
मनोऽनिलजवो भूत्वा गतोर्ध्वं चोर्ध्वतः पुरा ॥
2.1.m: Being extremely white, resembling fire, possessing wings on all sides, / and having the speed of the mind and the wind, I went up and up long ago.

2.1.s:
nārāyaṇo'pi viśvātmā suśveto hyabhavattadā |
daśayojanavistīrṇaṃ śatayojanamāyatam ||
2.1.d:
नारायणोऽपि विश्वात्मा सुश्वेतो ह्यभवत्तदा ।
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णं शतयोजनमायतम् ॥
2.1.m: Nārāyaṇa also, the Soul of the universe, became extremely white then, / ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long,

2.1.s:
meruparvatavarṣmāṇaṃ gauratīkṣṇogradaṃṣṭriṇam |
kālādityasamābhāsaṃ dīrghaghoṇaṃ mahāsvanam ||
2.1.d:
मेरुपर्वतवर्ष्माणं गौरतीक्ष्णोग्रदंष्ट्रिणम् ।
कालादित्यसमाभासं दीर्घघोणं महास्वनम् ॥
2.1.m: with a body like Mount Meru, having white, sharp, and fierce tusks, / resembling the sun of destruction, with a long snout and a mighty roar,

2.1.s:
hrasvapādaṃ vicitrāṅgaṃ jaitraṃ dṛḍhamanaupamam |
vārāhākāramāsthāya gatavāṃstadadhau javāt ||
2.1.d:
ह्रस्वपादं विचित्राङ्गं जैत्रं दृढमनौपमम् ।
वाराहाकारमास्थाय गतवांस्तदधौ जवात् ॥
2.1.m: short-legged, with variegated limbs, victorious, firm, and incomparable. / Assuming the form of a boar, he went beneath it with speed.

2.1.s:
evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca caranviṣṇuradho gataḥ |
tadāprabhṛti lokeṣu śvetavārāhasaṃjñakaḥ ||
2.1.d:
एवं वर्षसहस्रं च चरन्विष्णुरधो गतः ।
तदाप्रभृति लोकेषु श्वेतवाराहसंज्ञकः ॥
2.1.m: Moving thus for a thousand years, Viṣṇu went downward. / From that time on, among the worlds of men, the measure of time

2.1.s:
kalpo babhūva devarṣe narāṇāṃ kālasaṃjñakaḥ |
babhrāma bahudhā viṣṇuḥ prabhaviṣṇuradhogataḥ ||
2.1.d:
कल्पो बभूव देवर्षे नराणां कालसंज्ञकः ।
बभ्राम बहुधा विष्णुः प्रभविष्णुरधोगतः ॥
2.1.m: became the kalpa named Śvetavārāha, O divine sage. / Viṣṇu, the powerful lord, roamed about in many ways, having gone downward,

2.1.s:
nāpaśyadalpamapyasya mūlaṃ liṅgasya sūkaraḥ |
tāvatkālaṃ gataścordhvamahamapyarisūdana ||
2.1.d:
नापश्यदल्पमप्यस्य मूलं लिङ्गस्य सूकरः ।
तावत्कालं गतश्चोर्ध्वमहमप्यरिसूदन ॥
2.1.m: yet, as a boar, he did not see even the slightest base of this Liṅga. / For the same amount of time, I too went upwards, O slayer of foes,

2.1.s:
satvaraṃ sarvayatnena tasyāntaṃ jñātumicchayā |
śrānto na dṛṣṭvā tasyāntamahaṃ kālādadhogataḥ ||
2.1.d:
सत्वरं सर्वयत्नेन तस्यान्तं ज्ञातुमिच्छया ।
श्रान्तो न दृष्ट्वा तस्यान्तमहं कालादधोगतः ॥
2.1.m: hastily with all effort, wishing to know its end. / Weary, not seeing its end, in the course of time I came downward.

2.1.s:
tathaiva bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śrāntaḥ kamalalocanaḥ |
sarvadevanibhastūrṇamutthitaḥ sa mahāvapuḥ ||
2.1.d:
तथैव भगवान्विष्णुः श्रान्तः कमललोचनः ।
सर्वदेवनिभस्तूर्णमुत्थितः स महावपुः ॥
2.1.m: Likewise the blessed Lord Viṣṇu, lotus-eyed and weary, / who resembles all the gods, quickly rose up, having a vast body.

2.1.s:
samāgato mayā sārdhaṃ praṇipatya bhavaṃ muhuḥ |
māyayā mohitaḥ śambhostasthau saṃvignamānasaḥ ||
2.1.d:
समागतो मया सार्धं प्रणिपत्य भवं मुहुः ।
मायया मोहितः शम्भोस्तस्थौ संविग्नमानसः ॥
2.1.m: He met with me, repeatedly bowing down to Bhava; / deluded by the māyā of Śambhu, he stood with an agitated mind.

2.1.s:
pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvataścaiva hyagrataḥ parameśvaram |
praṇipatya mayā sārdhaṃ sasmāra kimidaṃ tviti ||
2.1.d:
पृष्ठतः पार्श्वतश्चैव ह्यग्रतः परमेश्वरम् ।
प्रणिपत्य मया सार्धं सस्मार किमिदं त्विति ॥
2.1.m: Bowing down to Parameśvara from behind, from the sides, and from the front, / he wondered together with me: "What is this?"

2.1.s:
anirdeśyaṃ ca tadrūpamanāma karmavarjitam |
aliṅgaṃ liṅgatāṃ prāptaṃ dhyānamārge'pyagocaram ||
2.1.d:
अनिर्देश्यं च तद्रूपमनाम कर्मवर्जितम् ।
अलिङ्गं लिङ्गतां प्राप्तं ध्यानमार्गेऽप्यगोचरम् ॥
2.1.m: That form was indefinable, nameless, devoid of actions, / markless, yet possessing the state of a Liṅga, beyond the reach of meditation.

2.1.s:
svasthaṃ cittaṃ tadā kṛtvā namaskāraparāyaṇau |
babhūvaturubhāvāvāmahaṃ harirapi dhruvam ||
2.1.d:
स्वस्थं चित्तं तदा कृत्वा नमस्कारपरायणौ ।
बभूवतुरुभावावामहं हरिरपि ध्रुवम् ॥
2.1.m: Then, composing our minds, both of us—I and Hari too— / surely became wholly devoted to bowing down in reverence:

2.1.s:
jānīvo na hi te rūpaṃ yo'si so'si mahāprabho |
namo'stu te maheśāna rūpaṃ darśaya nau tvaram ||
2.1.d:
जानीवो न हि ते रूपं योऽसि सोऽसि महाप्रभो ।
नमोऽस्तु ते महेशान रूपं दर्शय नौ त्वरम् ॥
2.1.m: "We do not know your form; whoever you are, so you are, O great Lord! / Homage be to you, O Maheśāna! Show your form to both of us swiftly."

2.1.s:
evaṃ śaracchatānyāsannamaskāraṃ prakurvatoḥ |
āvayormuniśārdūla madamāsthitayostadā ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaḥ sṛṣṭikhaṇḍaḥ
2.1.d:
एवं शरच्छतान्यासन्नमस्कारं प्रकुर्वतोः ।
आवयोर्मुनिशार्दूल मदमास्थितयोस्तदा ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां प्रथमः सृष्टिखण्डः
2.1.m:
Thus a hundred autumns passed for the two of us making prostrations, / O tiger among sages, having cast aside our arrogance then.

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "Description of the Dispute between Viṣṇu and Brahmā," in the Creation section of the second part, the Rudrasaṃhitā, of the glorious Śivapurāṇa.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
evaṃ tayormuniśreṣṭha darśanaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇayoḥ |
vigarvayośca surayoḥ sadā nau sthitayormune ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवं तयोर्मुनिश्रेष्ठ दर्शनं काङ्क्षमाणयोः ।
विगर्वयोश्च सुरयोः सदा नौ स्थितयोर्मुने ॥
2.1.m:
Brahmā said:
As the two of us were thus longing for the vision [of the Lord], O best of sages, / and remained standing there, two gods divested of our pride, O sage,

2.1.s:
dayālurabhavacchambhurdīnānāṃ pratipālakaḥ |
garviṇāṃ garvahartā ca sarveṣāṃ prabhuravyayaḥ ||
2.1.d:
दयालुरभवच्छम्भुर्दीनानां प्रतिपालकः ।
गर्विणां गर्वहर्ता च सर्वेषां प्रभुरव्ययः ॥
2.1.m: Śambhu, the protector of the humble, became compassionate— / the destroyer of the pride of the arrogant, the imperishable Lord of all.

2.1.s:
tadā samabhavattatra nādo vai śabdalakṣaṇaḥ |
omomiti suraśreṣṭhātsuvyaktaḥ plutalakṣaṇaḥ ||
2.1.d:
तदा समभवत्तत्र नादो वै शब्दलक्षणः ।
ओमोमिति सुरश्रेष्ठात्सुव्यक्तः प्लुतलक्षणः ॥
2.1.m: Then there arose in that place a sound characterized as audible speech, / distinctly uttering "Om, Om" from the greatest of gods, marked by a prolonged vowel.

2.1.s:
kimidaṃ tviti sañcintya mayā tiṣṭhanmahāsvanaḥ |
viṣṇuḥ sarvasurārādhyo nirvairastuṣṭacetasā ||
2.1.d:
किमिदं त्विति सञ्चिन्त्य मया तिष्ठन्महास्वनः ।
विष्णुः सर्वसुराराध्यो निर्वैरस्तुष्टचेतसा ॥
2.1.m: Thinking, "What indeed is this?", while that mighty sound continued, / Viṣṇu, who is worshipped by all gods, free from enmity and with a delighted mind,

2.1.s:
liṅgasya dakṣiṇe bhāge tathāpaśyatsanātanam |
ādyaṃ varṇamakārākhyamukāraṃ cottare tataḥ ||
2.1.d:
लिङ्गस्य दक्षिणे भागे तथापश्यत्सनातनम् ।
आद्यं वर्णमकाराख्यमुकारं चोत्तरे ततः ॥
2.1.m: saw in the southern part of the Liṅga the eternal, / primal syllable named "A"; and then "U" in the northern part;

2.1.s:
makāraṃ madhyataścaiva nādamante'sya comiti |
sūryamaṇḍalavad dṛṣṭvā varṇamādyaṃ tu dakṣiṇe ||
2.1.d:
मकारं मध्यतश्चैव नादमन्तेऽस्य चोमिति ।
सूर्यमण्डलवद् दृष्ट्वा वर्णमाद्यं तु दक्षिणे ॥
2.1.m: and "M" right in the middle, and the nasal sound at the end of it, making "Om". / Having seen that first syllable on the right, like the orb of the sun,

2.1.s:
uttare pāvakaprakhyamukāramṛṣisattama |
śītāṃśumaṇḍalaprakhyaṃ makāraṃ tasya madhyataḥ ||
2.1.d:
उत्तरे पावकप्रख्यमुकारमृषिसत्तम ।
शीतांशुमण्डलप्रख्यं मकारं तस्य मध्यतः ॥
2.1.m: the "U" on the left resembling fire, O best of sages, / and the "M" resembling the orb of the moon in its middle,

2.1.s:
tasyopari tadāpaśyacchuddhasphaṭikasuprabham |
turīyātītamamalaṃ niṣkalaṃ nirupadravam ||
2.1.d:
तस्योपरि तदापश्यच्छुद्धस्फटिकसुप्रभम् ।
तुरीयातीतममलं निष्कलं निरुपद्रवम् ॥
2.1.m: above it he then saw that which has the brilliant luster of pure crystal, / transcendent beyond the fourth state, immaculate, partless, free from afflictions,

2.1.s:
nirdvandvaṃ kevalaṃ śūnyaṃ bāhyābhyantaravarjitam |
sabāhyābhyantare caiva bāhyābhyantarasaṃsthitam ||
2.1.d:
निर्द्वन्द्वं केवलं शून्यं बाह्याभ्यन्तरवर्जितम् ।
सबाह्याभ्यन्तरे चैव बाह्याभ्यन्तरसंस्थितम् ॥
2.1.m: beyond dualities, absolute, empty, devoid of an outside and inside, / yet possessing both outside and inside, abiding in both the external and the internal.

2.1.s:
ādimadhyāntarahitamānandasyādikāraṇam |
satyamānandamamṛtaṃ paraṃ brahmaparāyaṇam ||
2.1.d:
आदिमध्यान्तरहितमानन्दस्यादिकारणम् ।
सत्यमानन्दममृतं परं ब्रह्मपरायणम् ॥
2.1.m: Devoid of beginning, middle, and end, the primal cause of bliss, / true, blissful, immortal, supreme, the highest resort of Brahman.

2.1.s:
kuta evātra sambhūtaḥ parīkṣāvo'gnisambhavam |
adho gamiṣyāmyanalastambhasyānupamasya ca ||
2.1.d:
कुत एवात्र सम्भूतः परीक्षावोऽग्निसम्भवम् ।
अधो गमिष्याम्यनलस्तम्भस्यानुपमस्य च ॥
2.1.m: "Whence indeed is this born here? Let us two examine the origin of the fire. / I will go to the bottom of this peerless pillar of fire."

2.1.s:
vedaśabdobhayāveśaṃ viśvātmānaṃ vyacintayat |
tadābhavadṛṣistatra ṛṣeḥ sāratamaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
2.1.d:
वेदशब्दोभयावेशं विश्वात्मानं व्यचिन्तयत् ।
तदाभवदृषिस्तत्र ऋषेः सारतमः स्मृतः ॥
2.1.m: He meditated upon the universal Self possessing both the sounds of the Veda. / Then a seer arose there, considered the quintessential among seers.

2.1.s:
tenaiva ṛṣiṇā viṣṇurjñātavānparameśvaram |
mahādevaṃ paraṃ brahma śabdabrahmatanuṃ param ||
2.1.d:
तेनैव ऋषिणा विष्णुर्ज्ञातवान्परमेश्वरम् ।
महादेवं परं ब्रह्म शब्दब्रह्मतनुं परम् ॥
2.1.m: Through that very seer, Viṣṇu came to know Parameśvara, / Mahādeva, the supreme Brahman, whose body is the sound-Brahman, the supreme.

2.1.s:
cintayā rahito rudro vāco yanmanasā saha |
aprāpya tannivartante vācyastvekākṣareṇa saḥ ||
2.1.d:
चिन्तया रहितो रुद्रो वाचो यन्मनसा सह ।
अप्राप्य तन्निवर्तन्ते वाच्यस्त्वेकाक्षरेण सः ॥
2.1.m: Rudra is free from anxiety; from whom words, together with the mind, / turn back having failed to reach [him]; but he is expressible by the single syllable.

2.1.s:
ekākṣareṇa tadvākyamṛtaṃ paramakāraṇam |
satyamānandamamṛtaṃ paraṃ brahma parātparam ||
2.1.d:
एकाक्षरेण तद्वाक्यमृतं परमकारणम् ।
सत्यमानन्दममृतं परं ब्रह्म परात्परम् ॥
2.1.m: Through that single syllable [comes] the utterance of him who is the immortal, the supreme cause, / true, blissful, immortal, the supreme Brahman, higher than the highest.

2.1.s:
ekākṣarādakārākhyādbhagavānbījako'ṇḍajaḥ |
ekākṣarādukārākhyāddhariḥ paramakāraṇam ||
2.1.d:
एकाक्षरादकाराख्याद्भगवान्बीजकोऽण्डजः ।
एकाक्षरादुकाराख्याद्धरिः परमकारणम् ॥
2.1.m: From the single syllable named "A" arose the lord who sows the seed, born from the egg; / from the single syllable named "U" arose Hari, the supreme cause.

2.1.s:
ekākṣarānmakārākhyādbhagavānnīlalohitaḥ |
sargakartā tvakārākhyo hyukārākhyastu mohakaḥ ||
2.1.d:
एकाक्षरान्मकाराख्याद्भगवान्नीललोहितः ।
सर्गकर्ता त्वकाराख्यो ह्युकाराख्यस्तु मोहकः ॥
2.1.m: From the single syllable named "M" arose the lord Nīlalohita; / the one named "A" is the creator of creation, while the one named "U" is the deluder.

2.1.s:
makārākhyastu yo nityamanugrahakaro'bhavat |
makārākhyo vibhurbījī hyakāro bīja ucyate ||
2.1.d:
मकाराख्यस्तु यो नित्यमनुग्रहकरोऽभवत् ।
मकाराख्यो विभुर्बीजी ह्यकारो बीज उच्यते ॥
2.1.m: The one named "M" is he who constantly bestows grace; / the all-pervading one named "M" is the possessor of the seed, while "A" is called the seed.

2.1.s:
ukārākhyo hariryoniḥ pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ |
bījī ca bījaṃ tadyonirnādākhyaśca maheśvaraḥ ||
2.1.d:
उकाराख्यो हरिर्योनिः प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः ।
बीजी च बीजं तद्योनिर्नादाख्यश्च महेश्वरः ॥
2.1.m: Hari, named "U", is the womb, the lord of Pradhāna and Puruṣa; / and the possessor of the seed, the seed, and that womb, and the one named Nāda, is Maheśvara.

2.1.s:
bījī vibhajya cātmānaṃ svecchayā tu vyavasthitaḥ |
asya liṅgādabhūd bījamakāro bījinaḥ prabhoḥ ||
2.1.d:
बीजी विभज्य चात्मानं स्वेच्छया तु व्यवस्थितः ।
अस्य लिङ्गादभूद् बीजमकारो बीजिनः प्रभोः ॥
2.1.m: Having divided himself by his own will, the possessor of the seed remained established; / from the liṅga of this lord, the possessor of the seed, arose the seed, the syllable "A".

2.1.s:
ukārayonau niḥkṣiptamavardhata samantataḥ |
sauvarṇamabhavaccāṇḍamāvedyaṃ tadalakṣaṇam ||
2.1.d:
उकारयोनौ निःक्षिप्तमवर्धत समन्ततः ।
सौवर्णमभवच्चाण्डमावेद्यं तदलक्षणम् ॥
2.1.m: Cast into the womb of the syllable "U", it grew on all sides; / and there arose a golden egg, to be made known, devoid of distinct attributes.

2.1.s:
anekābdaṃ tathā cāpsu divyamaṇḍaṃ vyavasthitam |
tato varṣasahasrānte dvidhā kṛtamajodbhavam ||
2.1.d:
अनेकाब्दं तथा चाप्सु दिव्यमण्डं व्यवस्थितम् ।
ततो वर्षसहस्रान्ते द्विधा कृतमजोद्भवम् ॥
2.1.m: Thus the divine egg remained in the waters for many years; / then, at the end of a thousand years, that which sprang from the Unborn was split into two.

2.1.s:
aṇḍamapsu sthitaṃ sākṣād vyāghāteneśvareṇa tu |
tathāsya suśubhaṃ haimaṃ kapālaṃ cordhvasaṃsthitam ||
2.1.d:
अण्डमप्सु स्थितं साक्षाद् व्याघातेनेश्वरेण तु ।
तथास्य सुशुभं हैमं कपालं चोर्ध्वसंस्थितम् ॥
2.1.m: The egg situated in the waters was struck directly by Īśvara; / and its auspicious, golden upper skull-half was situated above.

2.1.s:
jajñe sā dyaustadaparaṃ pṛthivī pañcalakṣaṇā |
tasmādaṇḍādbhavo jajñe kakārākhyaścaturmukhaḥ ||
2.1.d:
जज्ञे सा द्यौस्तदपरं पृथिवी पञ्चलक्षणा ।
तस्मादण्डाद्भवो जज्ञे ककाराख्यश्चतुर्मुखः ॥
2.1.m: That became heaven, and the other part became the earth having five characteristics; / from that egg was born Bhava, the four-faced one called the syllable "Ka".

2.1.s:
sa sraṣṭā sarvalokānāṃ sa eva trividhaḥ prabhuḥ |
evamomomiti proktamityāhuryajuṣāṃ varāḥ ||
2.1.d:
स स्रष्टा सर्वलोकानां स एव त्रिविधः प्रभुः ।
एवमोमोमिति प्रोक्तमित्याहुर्यजुषां वराः ॥
2.1.m: He is the creator of all worlds, he alone is the threefold lord; / in this way, it has been proclaimed as "Om, Om"—thus say the foremost of the Yajurvedins.

2.1.s:
yajuṣāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā ṛcaḥ sāmāni sādaram |
evameva hare brahmannityāhuścāvayostadā ||
2.1.d:
यजुषां वचनं श्रुत्वा ऋचः सामानि सादरम् ।
एवमेव हरे ब्रह्मन्नित्याहुश्चावयोस्तदा ॥
2.1.m: Having heard the word of the Yajurvedins, the Ṛgvedins and Sāmavedins respectfully / said to both of us at that time: "So it is indeed, O Hari, O Brahmā!"

2.1.s:
tato vijñāya deveśaṃ yathāvacchaktisambhavaiḥ |
mantrairmaheśvaraṃ devaṃ tuṣṭāva sumahodayam ||
2.1.d:
ततो विज्ञाय देवेशं यथावच्छक्तिसम्भवैः ।
मन्त्रैर्महेश्वरं देवं तुष्टाव सुमहोदयम् ॥
2.1.m: Then, having recognized the lord of gods, Viṣṇu duly praised / with mantras arising from his śakti the god Maheśvara of exceedingly great prosperity.

2.1.s:
etasminnantare'nyacca rūpamadbhutasundaram |
dadarśa ca mayā sārdhaṃ bhagavānviśvapālakaḥ ||
2.1.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरेऽन्यच्च रूपमद्भुतसुन्दरम् ।
ददर्श च मया सार्धं भगवान्विश्वपालकः ॥
2.1.m: Meanwhile, the lord, the protector of the universe, together with me, / beheld another wondrously beautiful form:

2.1.s:
pañcavaktraṃ daśabhujaṃ gaurakarpūravanmune |
nānākāntisamāyuktaṃ nānābhūṣaṇabhūṣitam ||
2.1.d:
पञ्चवक्त्रं दशभुजं गौरकर्पूरवन्मुने ।
नानाकान्तिसमायुक्तं नानाभूषणभूषितम् ॥
2.1.m: Having five faces and ten arms, resembling white camphor, O sage, / endowed with various splendors, adorned with various ornaments,

2.1.s:
mahodāraṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam |
taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtārtho'bhūnmayā hariḥ ||
2.1.d:
महोदारं महावीर्यं महापुरुषलक्षणम् ।
तं दृष्ट्वा परमं रूपं कृतार्थोऽभून्मया हरिः ॥
2.1.m: Exceedingly noble, of great valor, bearing the marks of a supreme cosmic person; / having seen that supreme form, Hari, along with me, felt fulfilled.

2.1.s:
atha prasanno bhagavānmaheśaḥ parameśvaraḥ |
divyaṃ śabdamayaṃ rūpamākhyāya prahasansthitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
अथ प्रसन्नो भगवान्महेशः परमेश्वरः ।
दिव्यं शब्दमयं रूपमाख्याय प्रहसन्स्थितः ॥
2.1.m: Then the gracious lord Maheśa, Parameśvara, / having revealed his divine form composed of sound, stood smiling.

2.1.s:
akārastasya mūrdhā hi lalāṭo dīrgha ucyate |
ikāro dakṣiṇaṃ netramīkāro vāmalocanam ||
2.1.d:
अकारस्तस्य मूर्धा हि ललाटो दीर्घ उच्यते ।
इकारो दक्षिणं नेत्रमीकारो वामलोचनम् ॥
2.1.m: The syllable "A" is indeed his crown, the long [vowel "Ā"] is said to be his forehead; / the syllable "I" is his right eye, and the syllable "Ī" his left eye.

2.1.s:
ukāro dakṣiṇaṃ śrotramūkāro vāma ucyate |
ṛkāro dakṣiṇaṃ tasya kapolaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ ||
2.1.d:
उकारो दक्षिणं श्रोत्रमूकारो वाम उच्यते ।
ऋकारो दक्षिणं तस्य कपोलं परमेष्ठिनः ॥
2.1.m: The syllable "U" is his right ear, and the syllable "Ū" is said to be his left; / the syllable "Ṛ" is the right cheek of the Supreme Lord.

2.1.s:
vāmaṃ kapolamṝkāro lṛ lṝ nāsāpuṭe ubhe |
ekāraścoṣṭha ūrdhvaśca hyaikārastvadharo vibhoḥ ||
2.1.d:
वामं कपोलमॄकारो लृ लॄ नासापुटे उभे ।
एकारश्चोष्ठ ऊर्ध्वश्च ह्यैकारस्त्वधरो विभोः ॥
2.1.m: The syllable "Ṝ" is his left cheek, and "Ḷ" and "Ḹ" are his two nostrils; / the syllable "E" is the upper lip, and "Ai" is the lower lip of the all-pervading lord.

2.1.s:
okāraśca tathaukāro dantapaṅktidvayaṃ kramāt |
amastu tālunī tasya devadevasya śūlinaḥ ||
2.1.d:
ओकारश्च तथौकारो दन्तपङ्क्तिद्वयं क्रमात् ।
अमस्तु तालुनी तस्य देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ॥
2.1.m: The syllable "O" and likewise "Au" are in order his two rows of teeth; / and the syllable "Aḥ" is the two palates of that god of gods who holds the trident.

2.1.s:
kādipañcākṣarāṇyasya pañca hastāśca dakṣiṇe |
cādipañcākṣarāṇyevaṃ pañca hastāstu vāmataḥ ||
2.1.d:
कादिपञ्चाक्षराण्यस्य पञ्च हस्ताश्च दक्षिणे ।
चादिपञ्चाक्षराण्येवं पञ्च हस्तास्तु वामतः ॥
2.1.m: The five syllables beginning with "Ka" are his five right hands; / and the five syllables beginning with "Ca" are his five hands on the left.

2.1.s:
ṭādipañcākṣaraṃ pādāstādi pañcākṣaraṃ tathā |
pakāra udaraṃ tasya phakāraḥ pārśva ucyate ||
2.1.d:
टादिपञ्चाक्षरं पादास्तादि पञ्चाक्षरं तथा ।
पकार उदरं तस्य फकारः पार्श्व उच्यते ॥
2.1.m: The five syllables beginning with "Ṭa" are his feet, and so are the five syllables beginning with "Ta"; / the syllable "Pa" is his belly, and the syllable "Pha" is said to be his flank.

2.1.s:
bakāro vāmapārśvastu bhakāraḥ skandha ucyate |
makāro hṛdayaṃ śambhormahādevasya yoginaḥ ||
2.1.d:
बकारो वामपार्श्वस्तु भकारः स्कन्ध उच्यते ।
मकारो हृदयं शम्भोर्महादेवस्य योगिनः ॥
2.1.m: The syllable "Ba" is his left flank, and the syllable "Bha" is said to be his shoulder; / the syllable "Ma" is the heart of Śambhu, of Mahādeva, the yogin.

2.1.s:
yakārādisakārāntā vibhorvai saptadhātavaḥ |
hakāro nābhirūpo hi kṣakāro ghrāṇa ucyate ||
2.1.d:
यकारादिसकारान्ता विभोर्वै सप्तधातवः ।
हकारो नाभिरूपो हि क्षकारो घ्राण उच्यते ॥
2.1.m: The syllables beginning with "Ya" and ending with "Sa" are indeed the seven bodily elements of the all-pervading lord; / the syllable "Ha" is in the form of his navel, and the syllable "Kṣa" is said to be his nose.

2.1.s:
evaṃ śabdamayaṃ rūpamaguṇasya guṇātmanaḥ |
dṛṣṭvā tamumayā sārdhaṃ kṛtārtho'bhūnmayā hariḥ ||
2.1.d:
एवं शब्दमयं रूपमगुणस्य गुणात्मनः ।
दृष्ट्वा तमुमया सार्धं कृतार्थोऽभून्मया हरिः ॥
2.1.m: Having thus seen the sound-composed form of the qualityless one whose essence is qualities, / and seeing him together with Umā, Hari along with me felt fulfilled.

2.1.s:
evaṃ dṛṣṭvā maheśānaṃ śabdabrahmatanuṃ śivam |
praṇamya ca mayā viṣṇuḥ punaścāpaśyadūrdhvataḥ ||
2.1.d:
एवं दृष्ट्वा महेशानं शब्दब्रह्मतनुं शिवम् ।
प्रणम्य च मया विष्णुः पुनश्चापश्यदूर्ध्वतः ॥
2.1.m: Having thus seen Maheśāna, Śiva whose body is the sound-Brahman, / and having bowed down along with me, Viṣṇu again looked upward.

2.1.s:
oṅkāraprabhavaṃ mantraṃ kalāpañcakasaṃyutam |
śuddhasphaṭikasaṅkāśaṃ śubhāṣṭatriṃśadakṣaram ||
2.1.d:
ओङ्कारप्रभवं मन्त्रं कलापञ्चकसंयुतम् ।
शुद्धस्फटिकसङ्काशं शुभाष्टत्रिंशदक्षरम् ॥
2.1.m: He saw the mantra originating from the syllable Oṃ, endowed with the five kalās, / resembling pure crystal, consisting of thirty-eight auspicious syllables,

2.1.s:
medhākāramabhūdbhūyaḥ sarvadharmārthasādhakam |
gāyatrīprabhavaṃ mantraṃ sahitaṃ vaśyakārakam ||
2.1.d:
मेधाकारमभूद्भूयः सर्वधर्मार्थसाधकम् ।
गायत्रीप्रभवं मन्त्रं सहितं वश्यकारकम् ॥
2.1.m: Which appeared as the form of intellect, accomplishing all aims of righteousness and wealth, / the mantra originating from the Gāyatrī, joined [with it], bringing subjugation,

2.1.s:
caturviṃśativarṇāḍhyaṃ catuṣkālamanuttamam |
atha pañcasitaṃ mantraṃ kalāṣṭakasamāyutam ||
2.1.d:
चतुर्विंशतिवर्णाढ्यं चतुष्कालमनुत्तमम् ।
अथ पञ्चसितं मन्त्रं कलाष्टकसमायुतम् ॥
2.1.m: Abounding in twenty-four syllables, encompassing four times, peerless. / Then [he saw] the five-fold white mantra endowed with eight kalās,

2.1.s:
ābhicārikamatyarthaṃ prāyastriṃśacchubhākṣaram |
yajurvedasamāyuktaṃ pañcaviṃśacchubhākṣaram ||
2.1.d:
आभिचारिकमत्यर्थं प्रायस्त्रिंशच्छुभाक्षरम् ।
यजुर्वेदसमायुक्तं पञ्चविंशच्छुभाक्षरम् ॥
2.1.m: Exceedingly incantatory, of approximately thirty auspicious syllables, / connected with the Yajurveda, possessing twenty-five auspicious syllables,

2.1.s:
kalāṣṭakasamāyuktaṃ suśvetaṃ śāntikaṃ tathā |
trayodaśakalāyuktaṃ bālādyaiḥ saha lehitam ||
2.1.d:
कलाष्टकसमायुक्तं सुश्वेतं शान्तिकं तथा ।
त्रयोदशकलायुक्तं बालाद्यैः सह लेहितम् ॥
2.1.m: Endowed with eight kalās, brilliant white, and pacifying; / endowed with thirteen kalās, savored together with children and others,

2.1.s:
babhūvurasya cotpattivṛddhisaṃhārakāraṇam |
varṇā ekādhikāḥ ṣaṣṭirasya mantravarasya tu ||
2.1.d:
बभूवुरस्य चोत्पत्तिवृद्धिसंहारकारणम् ।
वर्णा एकाधिकाः षष्टिरस्य मन्त्रवरस्य तु ॥
2.1.m: Which were the cause of his emergence, growth, and dissolution; / and sixty-one are the syllables of this excellent mantra.

2.1.s:
punarmṛtyuñjayaṃ mantraṃ pañcākṣaramataḥ param |
cintāmaṇiṃ tathā mantraṃ dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃjñakam ||
2.1.d:
पुनर्मृत्युञ्जयं मन्त्रं पञ्चाक्षरमतः परम् ।
चिन्तामणिं तथा मन्त्रं दक्षिणामूर्तिसंज्ञकम् ॥
2.1.m: Then [he saw] the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, and beyond this the five-syllabled mantra, / likewise the Cintāmaṇi mantra, and the one named Dakṣiṇāmūrti,

2.1.s:
tatastattvamasītyuktaṃ mahāvākyaṃ harasya ca |
pañcamantrāṃstathā labdhvā jajāpa bhagavānhariḥ ||
2.1.d:
ततस्तत्त्वमसीत्युक्तं महावाक्यं हरस्य च ।
पञ्चमन्त्रांस्तथा लब्ध्वा जजाप भगवान्हरिः ॥
2.1.m: And then the great utterance of Hara, spoken as "That thou art". / Having thus obtained the five mantras, the lord Hari chanted them.

2.1.s:
atha dṛṣṭvā kalāvarṇamṛgyajuḥsāmarūpiṇam |
īśānamīśamukuṭaṃ puruṣākhyaṃ purātanam ||
2.1.d:
अथ दृष्ट्वा कलावर्णमृग्यजुःसामरूपिणम् ।
ईशानमीशमुकुटं पुरुषाख्यं पुरातनम् ॥
2.1.m: Then, having seen him whose syllables are the kalās, who embodies the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman, / Īśāna, the crown of the Lord, the ancient one called Puruṣa,

2.1.s:
aghorahṛdayaṃ hṛdyaṃ sarvaguhyaṃ sadāśivam |
vāmapādaṃ mahādevaṃ mahābhogīndrabhūṣaṇam ||
2.1.d:
अघोरहृदयं हृद्यं सर्वगुह्यं सदाशिवम् ।
वामपादं महादेवं महाभोगीन्द्रभूषणम् ॥
2.1.m: Whose heart is Aghora, the delight of the heart, the all-secret Sadāśiva, / Mahādeva whose left foot is adorned with the great lord of serpents,

2.1.s:
viśvataḥ pādavantaṃ taṃ viśvato'kṣikaraṃ śivam |
brahmaṇo'dhipatiṃ sargasthitisaṃhārakāraṇam ||
2.1.d:
विश्वतः पादवन्तं तं विश्वतोऽक्षिकरं शिवम् ।
ब्रह्मणोऽधिपतिं सर्गस्थितिसंहारकारणम् ॥
2.1.m: Śiva who has feet on all sides, eyes and hands on all sides, / the ruler of Brahmā, the cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction,

2.1.s:
tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭābhiḥ sāmbaṃ varadamīśvaram |
mayā ca sahito viṣṇurbhagavāṃstuṣṭacetasā ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaḥ sṛṣṭikhaṇḍaḥ
2.1.d:
तुष्टाव वाग्भिरिष्टाभिः साम्बं वरदमीश्वरम् ।
मया च सहितो विष्णुर्भगवांस्तुष्टचेतसा ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां प्रथमः सृष्टिखण्डः
2.1.m:
The lord Viṣṇu, accompanied by me, with a contented heart, / praised the boon-granting Lord along with Ambikā with desirable words.

Thus ends the eighth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Body of the Sound-Brahman", in the Story of Creation, in the first section of the second Rudrasaṃhitā of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
athākarṇya nutiṃ viṣṇukṛtāṃ svasya maheśvaraḥ |
prādurbabhūva suprītaḥ savāmaḥ karuṇānidhiḥ ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
अथाकर्ण्य नुतिं विष्णुकृतां स्वस्य महेश्वरः ।
प्रादुर्बभूव सुप्रीतः सवामः करुणानिधिः ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / Then, having heard the praise offered to him by Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, / highly pleased, the treasure of compassion, manifested with his left half [Umā],

2.1.s:
pañcavaktrastrinayano bhālacandro jaṭādharaḥ |
gauravarṇo viśālākṣo bhasmoddhūlitavigrahaḥ ||
2.1.d:
पञ्चवक्त्रस्त्रिनयनो भालचन्द्रो जटाधरः ।
गौरवर्णो विशालाक्षो भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहः ॥
2.1.m: Five-faced, three-eyed, with the crescent moon on his forehead, matted-haired, / white-complexioned, large-eyed, his body smeared with ashes.

2.1.s:
daśabāhurnīlagalaḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ |
sarvāṅgasundaro bhasmatripuṇḍrāṅkitamastakaḥ ||
2.1.d:
दशबाहुर्नीलगलः सर्वाभरणभूषितः ।
सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरो भस्मत्रिपुण्ड्राङ्कितमस्तकः ॥
2.1.m: having ten arms, a blue neck, adorned with all ornaments, / handsome in all his limbs, his forehead marked with a tripuṇḍra of ashes.

2.1.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ devaṃ savāmaṃ parameśvaram |
tuṣṭāva punariṣṭābhirvāgbhirviṣṇurmayā saha ||
2.1.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा तादृशं देवं सवामं परमेश्वरम् ।
तुष्टाव पुनरिष्टाभिर्वाग्भिर्विष्णुर्मया सह ॥
2.1.m: Having seen that god of such a form, the Parameśvara accompanied by [his] left [half], / Viṣṇu, together with me, praised [him] again with agreeable words.

2.1.s:
nigamaṃ śvāsarūpeṇa dadau tasmai tato haraḥ |
viṣṇave ca prasannātmā maheśaḥ karuṇākaraḥ ||
2.1.d:
निगमं श्वासरूपेण ददौ तस्मै ततो हरः ।
विष्णवे च प्रसन्नात्मा महेशः करुणाकरः ॥
2.1.m: Then Hara, in the form of breath, gave the Veda to him, / to Viṣṇu—Maheśa, gracious in mind, the mine of compassion.

2.1.s:
tato jñānamadāttasmai rahasyaṃ paramātmane |
paramātmā punarmahyaṃ dattavānkṛpayā mune ||
2.1.d:
ततो ज्ञानमदात्तस्मै रहस्यं परमात्मने ।
परमात्मा पुनर्मह्यं दत्तवान्कृपया मुने ॥
2.1.m: Then he gave secret knowledge to that Paramātman; / and that Paramātman in turn gave [it] to me out of grace, O sage.

2.1.s:
samprāpya nigamaṃ viṣṇuḥ papraccha punareva tam |
kṛtārthaḥ sāñjalirnatvā mayā saha maheśvaram ||
viṣṇuruvāca |
kathaṃ ca tuṣyase deva mayā pūjyaḥ kathaṃ prabho |
kathaṃ dhyānaṃ prakartavyaṃ kathaṃ vrajasi vaśyatām | 8 ||
2.1.d:
सम्प्राप्य निगमं विष्णुः पप्रच्छ पुनरेव तम् ।
कृतार्थः साञ्जलिर्नत्वा मया सह महेश्वरम् ॥
विष्णुरुवाच ।
कथं च तुष्यसे देव मया पूज्यः कथं प्रभो ।
कथं ध्यानं प्रकर्तव्यं कथं व्रजसि वश्यताम् । 8 ॥
2.1.m:
Having received the Veda, Viṣṇu questioned him yet again, / fulfilled, with folded hands, having bowed down with me to Maheśvara.

Viṣṇu said: / And how are you pleased, O god? How are you to be worshipped by me, O Lord? / How should meditation be performed? How do you come under control? [8]

2.1.s:
kiṃ kartavyaṃ mahādeva hyāvābhyāṃ tava śāsanāt |
sadā sadājñāpaya nau prītyarthaṃ kuru śaṅkara ||
2.1.d:
किं कर्तव्यं महादेव ह्यावाभ्यां तव शासनात् ।
सदा सदाज्ञापय नौ प्रीत्यर्थं कुरु शङ्कर ॥
2.1.m: What is to be done, O Mahādeva, by the two of us at your command? / Always, always instruct the two of us; make [it] for [our] affection, O Śaṅkara.

2.1.s:
etatsarvaṃ mahārāja kṛpāṃ kṛtvāvayoḥ prabho |
kathanīyaṃ tathānyacca vijñāya svānugau śiva ||
2.1.d:
एतत्सर्वं महाराज कृपां कृत्वावयोः प्रभो ।
कथनीयं तथान्यच्च विज्ञाय स्वानुगौ शिव ॥
2.1.m: All this, O great king, having shown compassion to the two of us, O Lord, / is to be told, and other things too, knowing [us as] your followers, O Śiva.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā prasanno bhagavānharaḥ |
uvāca vacanaṃ prītyā suprasannaḥ kṛpānidhiḥ ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रसन्नो भगवान्हरः ।
उवाच वचनं प्रीत्या सुप्रसन्नः कृपानिधिः ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard this speech, the blessed Hara, well pleased, / very delighted, the treasure of compassion, spoke [these] words with love.

2.1.s:
śrīśiva uvāca |
bhaktyā ca bhavatornūnaṃ prīto'haṃ surasattamau |
paśyantaṃ māṃ mahādevaṃ bhayaṃ sarvaṃ vimuñcatām ||
2.1.d:
श्रीशिव उवाच ।
भक्त्या च भवतोर्नूनं प्रीतोऽहं सुरसत्तमौ ।
पश्यन्तं मां महादेवं भयं सर्वं विमुञ्चताम् ॥
2.1.m: The venerable Śiva said: / I am indeed pleased by the devotion of the two of you, O best of gods; / looking upon me, Mahādeva, cast away all fear.

2.1.s:
mama liṅgaṃ sadā pūjyaṃ dhyeyaṃ caitādṛśaṃ mama |
idānīṃ dṛśyate yadvattathā kāryaṃ prayatnataḥ ||
2.1.d:
मम लिङ्गं सदा पूज्यं ध्येयं चैतादृशं मम ।
इदानीं दृश्यते यद्वत्तथा कार्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥
2.1.m: My liṅga is always to be worshipped, and this form of mine is to be meditated upon; / just as it is seen now, so it should be made with effort.

2.1.s:
pūjito liṅgarūpeṇa prasanno vividhaṃ phalam |
dāsyāmi sarvalokebhyo mano'bhīṣṭānyanekaśaḥ ||
2.1.d:
पूजितो लिङ्गरूपेण प्रसन्नो विविधं फलम् ।
दास्यामि सर्वलोकेभ्यो मनोऽभीष्टान्यनेकशः ॥
2.1.m: Worshipped in the form of the liṅga, being pleased, I will bestow various fruits, / [and] the mind's desires in many ways, upon all worlds.

2.1.s:
yadā duḥkhaṃ bhavettatra yuvayoḥ surasattamau |
pūjite mama liṅge ca tadā syād duḥkhanāśanam ||
2.1.d:
यदा दुःखं भवेत्तत्र युवयोः सुरसत्तमौ ।
पूजिते मम लिङ्गे च तदा स्याद् दुःखनाशनम् ॥
2.1.m: Whenever suffering arises for the two of you there, O best of gods, / when my liṅga is worshipped, then destruction of suffering will occur.

2.1.s:
yuvāṃ prasūtau prakṛtermadīyāyā mahābalau |
savyāpasavyāgātrābhyāṃ mama sarveśvarasya hi ||
2.1.d:
युवां प्रसूतौ प्रकृतेर्मदीयाया महाबलौ ।
सव्यापसव्यागात्राभ्यां मम सर्वेश्वरस्य हि ॥
2.1.m: You two were born from my Prakṛti, O mighty ones, / from the left and right limbs of me, indeed the Lord of all.

2.1.s:
ayaṃ me dakṣiṇātpārśvād brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ |
vāmapārśvācca viṣṇustvaṃ samutpannaḥ parātmanaḥ ||
2.1.d:
अयं मे दक्षिणात्पार्श्वाद् ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
वामपार्श्वाच्च विष्णुस्त्वं समुत्पन्नः परात्मनः ॥
2.1.m: This Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, [was born] from my right side, / and you, Viṣṇu, were born from the left side of the Supreme Self.

2.1.s:
prīto'haṃ yuvayoḥ samyagvaraṃ dadyāṃ yathepsitam |
mayi bhaktirdṛḍhā bhūyādyuvayorabhyanujñayā ||
2.1.d:
प्रीतोऽहं युवयोः सम्यग्वरं दद्यां यथेप्सितम् ।
मयि भक्तिर्दृढा भूयाद्युवयोरभ्यनुज्ञया ॥
2.1.m: I am pleased with the two of you; I shall grant a boon according to your desire: / by [my] assent, let firm devotion to me exist in the two of you.

2.1.s:
pārthivīṃ caiva manmūrtiṃ vidhāya kurutaṃ yuvām |
sevāṃ ca vividhāṃ prājñau kṛtvā sukhamavāpsyathaḥ ||
2.1.d:
पार्थिवीं चैव मन्मूर्तिं विधाय कुरुतं युवाम् ।
सेवां च विविधां प्राज्ञौ कृत्वा सुखमवाप्स्यथः ॥
2.1.m: And having fashioned an earthen image of me, do you two perform / various services, O wise ones; having done [so], you will obtain happiness.

2.1.s:
brahmansṛṣṭiṃ kuru tvaṃ hi madājñāparipālakaḥ |
vatsa vatsa hare tvaṃ ca pālayaivaṃ carācaram ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मन्सृष्टिं कुरु त्वं हि मदाज्ञापरिपालकः ।
वत्स वत्स हरे त्वं च पालयैवं चराचरम् ॥
2.1.m: O Brahmā, do you carry out creation, obedient to my command; / child, dear Hari, do you in this way protect the moving and unmoving.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā nau prabhustābhyāṃ pūjāvidhimadācchubhām |
yenaiva pūjitaḥ śambhuḥ phalaṃ yacchatyanekaśaḥ ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा नौ प्रभुस्ताभ्यां पूजाविधिमदाच्छुभाम् ।
येनैव पूजितः शम्भुः फलं यच्छत्यनेकशः ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus to the two of us, the Lord gave an auspicious rule of worship, / by which alone Śambhu, when worshipped, grants fruits manifold.

2.1.s:
ityākarṇya vacaḥ śambhormayā ca sahito hariḥ |
pratyuvāca maheśānaṃ praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ ||
2.1.d:
इत्याकर्ण्य वचः शम्भोर्मया च सहितो हरिः ।
प्रत्युवाच महेशानं प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः ॥
2.1.m: Having heard this word of Śambhu, Hari, together with me, / replied to Maheśāna, bowing down with folded hands.

2.1.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
yadi prītiḥ samutpannā yadi deyo varaśca nau |
bhaktirbhavatu nau nityaṃ tvayi cāvyabhicāriṇī ||
2.1.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
यदि प्रीतिः समुत्पन्ना यदि देयो वरश्च नौ ।
भक्तिर्भवतु नौ नित्यं त्वयि चाव्यभिचारिणी ॥
2.1.m: Viṣṇu said: / If affection has arisen, if a boon is to be given to the two of us, / let devotion to you be ours always, and unswerving.

2.1.s:
tvamapyavatarasvādya līlayā nirguṇo'pi hi |
sahāyaṃ kuru nau tāta tvaṃ paraḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
2.1.d:
त्वमप्यवतरस्वाद्य लीलया निर्गुणोऽपि हि ।
सहायं कुरु नौ तात त्वं परः परमेश्वरः ॥
2.1.m: Do you also descend today as sport, even though qualityless; / grant help to us two, O father; you are the supreme Parameśvara.

2.1.s:
āvayordevadeveśa vivādamapi śobhanam |
ihāgato bhavānyasmādvivādaśamanāya nau ||
2.1.d:
आवयोर्देवदेवेश विवादमपि शोभनम् ।
इहागतो भवान्यस्माद्विवादशमनाय नौ ॥
2.1.m: Even the dispute between the two of us turned out well, O Lord of the gods of gods, / since you have come here for the calming of our dispute.

2.1.s:
brahmovāca |
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā punaḥ prāha haro harim |
praṇipatya sthitaṃ mūrdhnā kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ svayam ||
2.1.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पुनः प्राह हरो हरिम् ।
प्रणिपत्य स्थितं मूर्ध्ना कृताञ्जलिपुटः स्वयम् ॥
2.1.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard those words of his, Hara spoke again to Hari / who stood bowing with his head, his hands folded in reverence himself.

2.1.s:
śrīmaheśa uvāca |
pralayasthitisargāṇāṃ kartāhaṃ saguṇo'guṇaḥ |
parabrahma nirvikārī saccidānandalakṣaṇaḥ ||
2.1.d:
श्रीमहेश उवाच ।
प्रलयस्थितिसर्गाणां कर्ताहं सगुणोऽगुणः ।
परब्रह्म निर्विकारी सच्चिदानन्दलक्षणः ॥
2.1.m: The venerable Maheśa said: / I am the agent of dissolution, maintenance, and creation, with qualities and without qualities, / the supreme Brahman, changeless, having being, consciousness, and bliss as my definition.

2.1.s:
tridhā bhinno hyahaṃ viṣṇo brahmaviṣṇuharākhyayā |
sargarakṣālayaguṇairniṣkalo'haṃ sadā hare ||
2.1.d:
त्रिधा भिन्नो ह्यहं विष्णो ब्रह्मविष्णुहराख्यया ।
सर्गरक्षालयगुणैर्निष्कलोऽहं सदा हरे ॥
2.1.m: Indeed, I am threefold, O Viṣṇu, under the names Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Hara, / by the qualities of creation, protection, and dissolution, though I am partless always, O Hari.

2.1.s:
stuto'haṃ yattvayā viṣṇo brahmaṇā me'vatāraṇe |
prārthanāṃ tāṃ kariṣyāmi satyāṃ yadbhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.1.d:
स्तुतोऽहं यत्त्वया विष्णो ब्रह्मणा मेऽवतारणे ।
प्रार्थनां तां करिष्यामि सत्यां यद्भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.1.m: Since I was praised by you, O Viṣṇu, [and] by Brahmā for my descent, / I will make that prayer true, because I am affectionate toward devotees.

2.1.s:
madrūpaṃ paramaṃ brahmannīdṛśaṃ bhavadaṅgataḥ |
prakaṭībhavitā loke nāmnā rudraḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
2.1.d:
मद्रूपं परमं ब्रह्मन्नीदृशं भवदङ्गतः ।
प्रकटीभविता लोके नाम्ना रुद्रः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
2.1.m: This supreme form of mine, O Brahmā, shall become manifest in the world / from your body, renowned by the name Rudra.

2.1.s:
madaṃśāttasya sāmarthyaṃ nyūnaṃ naiva bhaviṣyati |
yo'haṃ so'haṃ na bhedo'sti pūjāvidhividhānataḥ ||
2.1.d:
मदंशात्तस्य सामर्थ्यं न्यूनं नैव भविष्यति ।
योऽहं सोऽहं न भेदोऽस्ति पूजाविधिविधानतः ॥
2.1.m: His capability will not be less at all, since he is a portion of mine; / he is who I am; there is no distinction according to the procedure of the rule of worship.

2.1.s:
yathā ca jyotiṣaḥ saṅgājjalādeḥ sparśatā na vai |
tathā mamāguṇasyāpi saṃyogād bandhanaṃ na hi ||
2.1.d:
यथा च ज्योतिषः सङ्गाज्जलादेः स्पर्शता न वै ।
तथा ममागुणस्यापि संयोगाद् बन्धनं न हि ॥
2.1.m: Just as there is no contact with water and the like from association with light, / so there is no bondage for me, though qualityless, from union [with qualities].

2.1.s:
śivarūpaṃ mamaitacca rudro'pi śivavattadā |
na tatra parabhedo vai kartavyaśca mahāmune ||
2.1.d:
शिवरूपं ममैतच्च रुद्रोऽपि शिववत्तदा ।
न तत्र परभेदो वै कर्तव्यश्च महामुने ॥
2.1.m: And this is my form as Śiva; Rudra too is then just like Śiva; / no difference of otherness is to be made there, O great sage.

2.1.s:
vastuto hyekarūpaṃ hi dvidhā bhinnaṃ jagatyuta |
ato bhedo na vijñeyaḥ śive rudre kadācana ||
2.1.d:
वस्तुतो ह्येकरूपं हि द्विधा भिन्नं जगत्युत ।
अतो भेदो न विज्ञेयः शिवे रुद्रे कदाचन ॥
2.1.m: For in reality it is one form, split into two in the world; / therefore, no difference is ever to be understood between Śiva and Rudra.

2.1.s:
suvarṇasya yathaikasya vastutvaṃ naiva gacchati |
alaṅkṛtikṛte deva nāmabhedo na vastutaḥ ||
2.1.d:
सुवर्णस्य यथैकस्य वस्तुत्वं नैव गच्छति ।
अलङ्कृतिकृते देव नामभेदो न वस्तुतः ॥
2.1.m: Just as the substance of gold alone does not perish / when it is made into an ornament, O god, there is a difference in name, not in reality;

2.1.s:
yathaikasyā mṛdo bhedo nānāpātre na vastutaḥ |
kāraṇasyaiva kārye na sannidhānaṃ nidarśanam ||
2.1.d:
यथैकस्या मृदो भेदो नानापात्रे न वस्तुतः ।
कारणस्यैव कार्ये न सन्निधानं निदर्शनम् ॥
2.1.m: just as there is no difference in reality in various vessels made of one clay, / the cause alone being present in the effect, as an illustration;

2.1.s:
jñātavyaṃ budhavaryaiśca nirmalajñānibhiḥ surau |
evaṃ jñātvā bhavadbhyāṃ tu na dṛśyaṃ bhedakāraṇam ||
2.1.d:
ज्ञातव्यं बुधवर्यैश्च निर्मलज्ञानिभिः सुरौ ।
एवं ज्ञात्वा भवद्भ्यां तु न दृश्यं भेदकारणम् ॥
2.1.m: so is it to be understood by the best of the wise and by those of stainless knowledge, O gods; / knowing this, a cause of difference should not be seen by you two.

2.1.s:
vastuvat sarvadṛśyaṃ ca śivarūpaṃ mataṃ mama |
ahaṃ bhavānajaścaiva rudro yo'yaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
2.1.d:
वस्तुवत् सर्वदृश्यं च शिवरूपं मतं मम ।
अहं भवानजश्चैव रुद्रो योऽयं भविष्यति ॥
2.1.m: Like the reality, all that is seen is considered by me to be the form of Śiva; / I, you, the unborn [Brahmā], and this Rudra who will come to be—

2.1.s:
ekarūpā na bhedastu bhede vai bandhanaṃ bhavet |
tathāpi ca madīyaṃ hi śivarūpaṃ sanātanam ||
2.1.d:
एकरूपा न भेदस्तु भेदे वै बन्धनं भवेत् ।
तथापि च मदीयं हि शिवरूपं सनातनम् ॥
2.1.m: [all] are of one form, and there is no distinction; if there is distinction, there would indeed be bondage; / even so, my form as Śiva is eternal,

2.1.s:
mūlībhūtaṃ sadoktaṃ ca satyajñānamanantakam |
evaṃ jñātvā sadā dhyeyaṃ manasā caiva tattvataḥ ||
2.1.d:
मूलीभूतं सदोक्तं च सत्यज्ञानमनन्तकम् ।
